items.title: Hindsight Is 2024
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. When Donald Trump returned to the White House in 2025, he was nursing grudges and claiming a mandate. The institutions he saw as his enemies—in politics, business, and education—faced a dilemma about how to respond. A few concluded that they should resist the president’s demands of fealty and collaboration. Another group tried appeasement , seeking accommodation that would allow them to otherwise operate as usual. And some looked at the landscape and concluded that something fundamental had shifted in American politics. They saw the MAGA movement as a lasting change, and decided that their best move was to make their own radical shift to adjust. As I wrote last week , predictions of a Trump-driven realignment of the electorate now look extremely shaky. The groups that he was able to attract to the Republican ticket two years ago—young voters, especially men; Hispanic voters; and Black men—have turned solidly against him and against GOP candidates in polls ahead of the midterms. Voters who were unimpressed with Joe Biden or Kamala Harris and who heard Trump’s promise of stopping inflation are now angry about the president’s shrugging at higher prices and inflationary war in Iran. With some distance, the 2024 election looks less like a decisive turning point and more like a fluke. But that realization has come too late for those who reshaped themselves for a reality that has proved ephemeral. David Ellison, who, along with his father, Larry, is a friend of Trump’s, decided to use the new Trump administration as an opportunity to build a huge media conglomerate. First, his company Skydance merged with Paramount. Taking control of CBS News, he installed Bari Weiss as editor in chief, seeking a leader who would appeal more to both the White House and to conservative viewers. But Weiss’s makeover has so far looked like a flop: 60 Minutes has hemorrhaged staffers, and the Evening News has hemorrhaged viewers. Her proposition was that a slightly more conservative version of the mainstream media would bring the audience back to a struggling network, but that doesn’t appear to actually be appealing to either MAGA viewers or legacy CBS watchers. Ellison has already moved on to an attempted merger with Warner Bros., reportedly promising administration officials deep political changes at CNN if the deal was approved by federal regulators. Ellison got approval, but now that deal is in trouble anyway. Facing an antitrust lawsuit led by the attorney general of California, Paramount agreed to pause the merger until a trial next year. Experts are divided on how likely Paramount is to prevail, but if the merger doesn’t close by September 30, the company will owe Warner Bros. shareholders $7 million every day until it does. In a New York Times column last week, Ellison complained that people are drawing incorrect inferences about his politics, but his private views are beside the point: What is public is Ellison’s willingness to play to the Trump administration’s politics to build an empire. CBS News is not the only media interest to discover that courting MAGA news consumers is not a guarantee of success or growth. The Times also reported recently on how a range of right-wing influencers has seen audiences shrink drastically. Their travails appear to reflect Trump’s own difficulty in keeping his 2024 coalition together: The most pro-Trump figures have seen some of the biggest drops, amid ideological battles inside the MAGA coalition over Israel and the war in Iran, while more Trump-critical figures on the right have sometimes gained. Other corporate leaders also bet on Trump. Elon Musk attempted to become something like an unelected deputy president at the start of Trump’s second term. That experiment ended acrimoniously, and the men’s relationship has been on and off ever since, but Musk’s reputation is now inextricably connected with Trump’s. X has shed users. Tesla sales have struggled, in part because anti-Trump consumers have turned against Musk and also because Musk has been distracted by other ventures, such as SpaceX. These decisions to throw in with Trump were notable because many institutions treated his 2016 win as an accident of chance , and were happy to publicly resist him. In doing so, though, they seem to have opened the door to more direct corporate involvement in politics—and with it, greater vulnerability to political pressure. The idea that corporations had gone “woke” by embracing DEI and other progressive causes in 2020 and 2021 was to some extent a marketing ploy by the companies , but it infuriated Republicans and made them targets for Trump’s second administration. Trying to protect themselves, corporate leaders now may have overcorrected, mistakenly assuming a lasting MAGA regime. Within right-wing politics, many individuals and organizations also leapt into Trumpism. The venerable Heritage Foundation reworked itself and lost or pushed out many long-standing scholars and staffers. Now it finds itself in an identity crisis —and also shut out of the White House because Trump is still sore about the attention and credit that Project 2025 won for driving his agenda. Many mainstream Republicans remade themselves as MAGA Republicans, but the results have not always been good. Just ask Senator John Cornyn, who lost his primary to an even-more-MAGA challenger this May. Earlier this month, Politico ’s Kathy Gilsinan reported on the broken pipeline for bringing new foot soldiers into conservative government and nonprofit organizations. “Everyone knows what the problem is: The organizations that bring young staffers to Washington, D.C. have spent the last decade prioritizing blind ideological loyalty instead of competence or intelligence,” a senior GOP congressional staffer told her. “We have a generation of rabid, incompetent idiots.” This is the risk of betting big on a long-term realignment: If you wager wrong, politics overall will snap back quickly, but you will be stuck with the consequences of your decision for much longer. Related: Americans are turning on Trump. What if 2016 was a fluke? ( From 2020 ) Here are three new stories from The Atlantic : Tyler Austin Harper on why he quit the tenure track The man in charge of immigration data just resigned. Charles Fain Lehman : In defense of Flock Today’s News A 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck western Colombia, killing at least 111 people and causing building collapses, injuries, and widespread damage , according to Colombian officials. President Trump told Axios that the United States is only “semi-negotiating” with Iran as talks over reopening the Strait of Hormuz remain stalled after Tehran laid out its demands, including compensation for war damage. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected the Trump administration’s 15-point Gaza plan yesterday , saying that Israel will not withdraw its forces until Hamas is fully disarmed. The proposal, announced by Trump’s Board of Peace last month, called for Hamas to surrender its weapons in phases in exchange for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Gaza. Dispatches The Weekly Planet : Living outside is a more dreadful prospect during a heat wave, Meg Bernhard reports. Explore all of our newsletters here. Evening Read Illustration by Lucy Murray Willis / The Atlantic If Only This Could Last Forever By Elizabeth Bruenig Summer always overstays its welcome by about a month. After the Fourth of July, which has its charms, nothing but a stretch of relentless heat lies ahead, reaching toward Labor Day, and I begin to yearn for fall. So does the grand, semi-malevolent intelligence that organizes American consumption: By mid-August, grocery stores are stocking their shelves with autumnal goods—pumpkin-pie Pop-Tarts, cinnamon-maple Frosted Flakes, pumpkin-spice cinnamon rolls in pressurized cardboard tubes. As I stroll through the aisles, I gaze wistfully at candy corn while the frosty supermarket air cools the sweat I worked up walking to the store beneath the blazing sun. Late September can’t arrive soon enough. Read the full article. The watchdogs are barking themselves hoarse. Ukraine may be just the ally America needs. Culture Break Illustration by Pedro Nekoi Explore. Are raccoons evolving into pets? items.title: Corporate Ghana, international community present relief donations to government following June 29 disaster
items.description: Corporate organisations and institutions have donated cash, food, medical supplies and other essential items to support victims of the June 29, 2026 flood disaster. The donations were presented to the Office of the President as part of ongoing efforts to provide relief to communities affected by the torrential rains and flooding, particularly in Accra. Senior government officials, including Deputy Chief of Staff (Administration), Nana Oye Bampoe Addo; Legal Advisor to the President, Marietta Brew; and Presidential Adviser and Special Aide, Joyce Bawa Mogtari, received the donations on behalf of the government. Two organisations also presented cash contributions towards the relief effort. SoftCare FM Manufacturing Company Limited donated GH¢200,000, while the Ghana Institute of Surveyors contributed GH¢50,000. Among the largest donations was a package from the Ghana Association of Chinese Societies and Companies, which provided a wide range of food, medical and household supplies. The donation included 1,112 bags of rice, 4,000 bags of sachet water, 500 cartons of sunflower oil, 490 cartons of Frytol oil, 490 cartons of canned mackerel, 646 cartons of gari and 501 cartons of spaghetti . The association also donated 295 cartons of sardines, 235 cartons of biscuits, 208 cartons of tomato paste, 50 cartons of shito and other provisions. Its medical and sanitation supplies included 2,000 malaria rapid test kits, 800 HPV test kits, anti-malaria medication, hand sanitiser and disinfectant. The relief package further included 3,000 sleeping mats, 400 school bags, 3,200 T-shirts, 3,100 plastic buckets, 3,000 plastic basins and five 2,000-litre stainless steel water tanks. The association also supplied chest freezers, electric cookers, electric fans, shovels, mosquito coils and temporary shelter and bedding materials. Other major donations Scancom Plc (MTN Ghana), supported by the Multimedia Group’s flood relief campaign, donated 1,400 student mattresses, 1,192 blankets and 998 relief boxes containing food items, blankets, mosquito repellents, mosquito nets and detergents. Sentuo Group Limited contributed 4,000 bags of 25kg rice, 600 bags of 50kg sugar and 387 boxes of granular maize . Ecobank Ghana donated medicines and other medical supplies, alongside 1,000 bags of sachet water, 195 mattresses, 250 blankets and bales of used clothing for men, women and children. Softcare FM Manufacturing Company Limited also donated 100 bags of washing powder, 100 boxes of soap, 100 boxes of sanitary pads and 50 boxes of baby diapers. B5 Plus Limited contributed 70 bags of 50kg rice, 100 bags of 50kg maize, 50 cartons of Cerelac, 75 jerrycans of cooking oil, sardines, bottled water and other relief items. Its donation also included 200 blankets, 200 two-litre jerrycans, 150 mosquito nets, 100 pairs of Wellington boots and 100 raincoats. Eezzy Group donated rice, spaghetti, canned beef, sardines, tomato paste, cooking oil, seasoning powders and baking supplies. Tobinco Group provided 100 boxes of Omal antiseptic, 5,000 gallons of Omal liquid soap and 400 gallons of Omazone bleach. Kam Trading & Farms Limited also contributed 445 bags of 25kg rice. The donations form part of a wider response to the devastating flooding of June 29, which left several communities in Accra and other parts of the country severely affected. The government has since been coordinating relief and recovery efforts, while corporate organisations, civil society groups and other institutions have mobilised resources to support affected households. The latest contributions are expected to help provide immediate necessities, including food, clean water, medicines, bedding, sanitation products and other household items, as affected communities work towards recovery.

items.title: L’Algérie entame le retrait de la circulation des bus de 30 ans
items.description: L’Algérie lance une vaste opération de retrait des bus de transport urbain âgés de 30 ans et plus. Les Directions de transports des wilayas ont lancé le processus de remplacement de ces véhicules. À Alger, la direction des transports de la wilaya a demandé aux transporteurs ayant des bus âgés de 30 ans et plus (jusqu’à 1996) de se rapprocher de ses services pour déposer le dossier de renouvellement. Ce dernier comprend une demande de substitution d’un bus usagé par un neuf, la carte grise, la fiche d'itinéraire ou la carte de parcours originale et la décision d’exploitation originale. En échange, le propriétaire du bus reçoit un « certificat de dépôt pour la mise au rebut du véhicule ancien auprès de la Société nationale de récupération de valorisation (SNRV) ». Une remise de 20 % sur le prix du bus neuf Un second certificat, permettant au client de finaliser les démarches d'acquisition du bus, notamment par financement bancaire auprès d'un opérateur agréé, sera délivré après présentation d'un document officiel attestant le dépôt du véhicule auprès de la Société Nationale de Recyclage des Ferrailleurs. La Direction des transports d’Alger précise que les clients bénéficient de nouveaux avantages spécifiques pour l’acquisition d’un nouveau bus. Il s’agit d’une remise de 20 % sur le prix du véhicule, de la possibilité d’obtenir un crédit bancaire avec un apport personnel de 10 % et une période de remboursement qui s’étale sur 10 ans. L’Algérie a décidé de retirer de la circulation des bus usagés de plus de 25 ans après l’accident tragique d’El Harrach il y a près d’une année. Le 15 août 2025, un bus a sauté du haut d’un pont dans l’oued qui porte le nom de ce quartier populaire d’Alger. Bilan : 18 morts et 25 blessés. Pour remplacer les vieux bus, polluants et peu sûrs, l’Algérie a importé 10.000 bus neufs. L’article L’Algérie entame le retrait de la circulation des bus de 30 ans est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: San : l’armée repousse une attaque malgré des pertes
items.description: © San Une attaque a été perpétrée dimanche 9 août contre l’emprise du 23 e Régiment d’infanterie de San. L’État-major général des Armées affirme avoir repris le contrôle du camp après des combats ayant fait des victimes dans les rangs militaires et parmi les assaillants. Selon le communiqué publié lundi 10 août, l’attaque a débuté vers 5 h 30 et a mobilisé des mitrailleuses lourdes, des drones kamikazes, des drones largueurs de charges ainsi que deux véhicules blindés. L’un de ces véhicules a permis l’ouverture d’une brèche dans le mur de clôture, facilitant l’infiltration d’assaillants dans l’emprise. L’État-major indique que la riposte des unités en défense a permis de repousser l’offensive, de neutraliser plusieurs combattants infiltrés et de « rétablir le contrôle de l’emprise ». Les premières évaluations militaires font état de plus d’une cinquantaine d’assaillants neutralisés et de nombreux blessés qui auraient été emportés lors du repli. Concernant les FAMa, le communiqué précise que l’État-major « s’incline devant la mémoire des militaires tombés au champ d’honneur », présente ses condoléances à leurs familles et à leurs frères d’armes et souhaite « un prompt rétablissement aux blessés ». Les opérations de recherche et de poursuite se sont poursuivies après le retrait des assaillants. Dans une communication publiée la veille, l’armée avait également indiqué qu’un groupe ayant participé à l’attaque avait été localisé à 17 kilomètres de San, poursuivi puis neutralisé, avec une partie de son matériel détruite et l’autre récupérée. Le camp de San, inauguré en octobre 2024, abrite le 23 e Régiment d’infanterie et constitue l’une des principales installations militaires de cette partie du centre du Mali. L’attaque intervient dans un contexte de multiplication des opérations contre les positions militaires, tandis que les FAMa poursuivent leurs opérations de sécurisation dans plusieurs régions du pays.

items.title: 2027: Kwankwaso rejects Jingir’s call for Muslim-Muslim ticket
items.description: Former Kano State governor and 2023 presidential candidate of the New Nigeria Peoples Party (NNPP), Rabiu Kwankwaso, has condemned comments by Islamic cleric, Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir, in support of the continued adoption of Muslim-Muslim presidential tickets ahead of the 2027 general elections. Kwankwaso, in a statement posted on his official X account on Monday, described Jingir’s remarks as divisive and urged political and religious leaders to promote unity and reconciliation. “I am deeply concerned by the comments made by Sheikh Sani Yahaya Jingir at an event in Kano this weekend. At this critical moment in our nation’s history, statements that promote division and disunity must be firmly discouraged,” he said. Jingir had sparked debate after advocating the continued use of Muslim-Muslim presidential tickets ahead of the 2027 election. The cleric made the remarks at an event attended by some All Progressives Congress governors, including Kano State Governor Abba Yusuf and his Jigawa State counterpart, Umar Namadi, according to a video circulating on Sunday. Jingir praised President Bola Tinubu for adopting the Muslim-Muslim ticket in the 2023 presidential election and said he remained a strong supporter of the arrangement. Reacting, Kwankwaso said religious and political leaders had a responsibility to avoid statements capable of deepening divisions in the country. “It is particularly troubling to hear such rhetoric from a religious leader of Sheikh Jingir’s stature and influence,” the former governor said. He added that the people of Kano did not support the cleric’s remarks. “Let it be clearly stated: the good people of Kano do not endorse or support these divisive remarks. Political and religious leaders alike carry a solemn responsibility to uphold truth, foster unity, and advance reconciliation,” Kwankwaso said. He also said the 2027 election would provide Nigerians with an opportunity to assess the performance of the current administration through the ballot box. “The 2027 general elections will be an opportunity for Nigerians to reward good governance with resounding support and to reject poor performance at the polls. This administration has earned the latter,” he said. The post 2027: Kwankwaso rejects Jingir’s call for Muslim-Muslim ticket appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Chery enters global top 10 wales, surpasses 20m vehicle sales
items.description: *As Carloha celebrates feat By Theodore Opara Carloha Nigeria, authorised distributor of Chery vehicles in Nigeria, has celebrated another landmark achievement by Chery Automobile as the global automotive brand continues its remarkable ascent on the world stage. Following Chery’s historic achievement of surpassing 20 million cumulative global vehicle sales, the company has now reached another significant milestone by entering the top 10 global automakers sales league for the first time. According to Chery Automobile Executive Vice President, Li Xueyong, Chery now ranks ninth globally with a 4.1% market share, tying with Ford, while becoming one of the three Chinese automakers to feature in the global top ten—an achievement that reflects the growing global influence of China’s automotive industry. The latest accomplishment further reinforces Chery’s transformation from a domestic Chinese manufacturer into one of the world’s fastest-growing automotive brands, with approximately one-third of its global sales generated from international markets. The company’s expanding footprint across Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Asia-Pacific, and Latin America continues to demonstrate increasing consumer confidence in the Chery brand. Chery’s export business has become the primary engine of its global growth. In July 2026, the company exported more than 202,500 vehicles, becoming the first Chinese automobile manufacturer to exceed 200,000 vehicle exports in a single month. The achievement also marked the fifth consecutive month that Chery has set a new monthly export record for China’s automotive industry, underscoring its leadership in global automotive exports. According to Carloha Nigeria, these milestones further validate the increasing acceptance of Chery’s innovative products, advanced engineering, and intelligent mobility technologies among motorists worldwide. “Surpassing 20 million global vehicle sales and now joining the world’s Top 10 automakers represent defining moments in Chery’s global journey,”said Felix Mahan, General Manager, Marketing, Carloha Nigeria.”These achievements demonstrate Chery’s unwavering commitment to innovation, quality, safety, and customer satisfaction. For our customers in Nigeria, they provide even greater confidence that they are investing in a globally trusted automotive brand that continues to set new benchmarks in the international automotive industry.” Over the years, Chery has earned international recognition for producing technologically advanced vehicles that combine premium design, intelligent safety features, outstanding performance, and exceptional value. Continuous investment in research and development, New Energy Vehicles (NEVs), intelligent connectivity, and advanced manufacturing has enabled the company to compete successfully alongside some of the world’s leading automotive brands. In Nigeria, Carloha continues to strengthen Chery’s presence by offering an expanding portfolio of premium SUVs and New Energy Vehicles, supported by a comprehensive after-sales ecosystem that delivers exceptional ownership value. Customers benefit from the exclusive CarlohaCare 6-6-7 ownership package, comprising a 6-year vehicle warranty, 6 years of complimentary scheduled servicing (including labour and genuine parts), and a 7-day repair promise, which provides customers with a courtesy vehicle if repairs exceed seven days. The company also offers CarlohaCare 6-6-7 Rescue, a free24-hour emergency roadside assistance service available nationwide for Chery owners, with limited support extended to non-Chery motorists. As Chery expands its presence across more than 110 countries and regions, Carloha Nigeria remains committed to bringing world-class mobility solutions, cutting-edge automotive technologies, and premium customer experiences to Nigerian motorists. “Chery’s continued global success reflects the strength of its long-term vision and relentless pursuit of excellence,”Mahan added. “Carloha Nigeria remains committed to ensuring that Nigerian customers benefit from globally acclaimed vehicles backed by exceptional after-sales support and an ownership experience that truly distinguishes the Chery brand.” With record-breaking global sales, unprecedented export performance, and its new position among the world’s Top 10 automakers, Chery is well positioned to shape the future of the global automotive industry while delivering greater value, innovation, and sustainable mobility solutions to customers worldwide. items.title: 2027: Umahi dismisses opposition to APC Muslim-Muslim ticket
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — The Minister of Works, Engr. David Umahi, has dismissed opposition to the All Progressives Congress, APC, Muslim-Muslim presidential ticket, urging Nigerians to focus on performance rather than religion. Umahi spoke on Monday when members of the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, paid him a courtesy visit in Abuja. His comments came amid controversy over recent remarks by Jos-based Islamic cleric, Sheikh Yahaya Jingir, and reactions from Nigeria’s Ambassador to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode, former Minister of Youth and Sports Development, Solomon Dalung, and others. Umahi said religion should not be used as a basis for assessing the performance of government officials. “What has religion got to do with performance? If we agree that we are brothers and sisters, forget about your religion. Because nobody intentionally chose a religion. It is based on worshipping God. And we are all created by the same God,” he said. “But when people don’t know what to talk about, they begin to talk about mundane things. They begin to become sentimental.” The minister urged Nigerian students to actively support President Bola Tinubu’s administration, particularly its reforms in the education sector. He also challenged students to defend what they consider the achievements of the administration whenever they encounter what he described as false narratives on social media. “This is the time to take sides in our national affairs,” Umahi said. He cited several ongoing road projects as evidence of the administration’s performance, including the Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano Superhighway, which he said covers 375 kilometres in each direction. “We have spent over $200 million on that project. Over 80 per cent has been paid. We are believing that by November, the entire stretch will have been completed,” he said. Umahi also cited the 350-kilometre Sokoto-Zamfara road project, valued at about $800 million; the 260-kilometre Benue-9th Mile road project, valued at $959 million; and the 39.7-kilometre Port Harcourt road project, valued at $280 million. He said the Federal Government had also approved a new flyover on the Benue-9th Mile route to address safety concerns. On education, the minister claimed that industrial actions in tertiary institutions had reduced under the Tinubu administration, saying, “For the first time, students never went on strike. Never. Look at the stability of the nation. Never happened in the history of this country.” He further claimed that inflation was declining, citing the price of a 50kg bag of rice, which he said had fallen from more than N80,000 in 2023 to about N55,000. “The worst is over,” Umahi said. The minister said President Tinubu should not be blamed for poor performance in any sector, arguing that the President had delegated responsibilities to ministers and other appointees. “The President has divided himself into a number of his appointees. Blame us and not the President when things are not going well. That is leadership,” he said. Earlier, the NANS President, Comrade Babatunde Akinteye, commended Umahi for what he described as visionary leadership and delivery of road infrastructure across the country. Akinteye said the students’ visit was to recognise Umahi’s contributions to national development and the impact of road infrastructure on students. “For students, infrastructure is not an abstract concept. A bad road can mean arriving late for examination. A bad road can increase the cost of your transportation to school,” he said. He added that an efficient road network could connect students to institutions, internships, businesses, jobs and the wider economy. Akinteye listed projects including the Abuja-Kaduna Expressway, Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano road, Enugu-Onitsha Expressway and the 3,000-kilometre coastal corridor as among projects under Umahi’s supervision. He also highlighted the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway and Lagos-Sokoto Road, describing them as landmark projects capable of improving connectivity and economic activity across the country. items.title: Homicide involontaire : 1 an d’emprisonnement et 1 million de GNF requis contre Ibrahima Kalil Tounkara
items.description: Le procureur près le tribunal de première instance de Dixinn a requis, ce lundi 10 août 2026, la condamnation d’Ibrahima Kalil Tounkara à un (1) an d’emprisonnement et au paiement d’une amende d’un (1) million de francs guinéens pour homicide involontaire. Courant 2026, ce menuisier de profession a mortellement fauché Mafory Touré dans un accident de la circulation à moto, au quartier Kénien, situé dans la commune de Dixinn. Le prévenu n’a pas nié les faits qui lui sont reprochés, mais a expliqué qu’il avait posé cet acte involontairement et a exprimé ses regrets. « Je reconnais les faits qui me sont reprochés. Je quittais mon lieu de travail, arrivé au niveau de Kenien, un camion était garé devant moi, la vieille en tentant de traverser est sortie brusquement devant moi. Je l’ai percuté et elle est tombée. On l’a transporté au CHU d’Ignace Deen où elle a rendu l’âme », a expliqué le prévenu. À la suite de cette narration, plusieurs questions lui ont été posées aussi bien par le tribunal que par le procureur. C’est entre autres, son niveau de maîtrise, la défaillance du système de freinage, mais Ibrahima Kalil Tounkara a réitéré que l’accident causé à feue Mafory Touré était indépendant de sa volonté. « Depuis 2018 je conduis la moto et c’est la première fois que cela m’arrive. Monsieur le procureur, je ne cesse de me rappeler de cette scène même étant seul. Je le regrette et je demande pardon, je n’ai pas fais expres », a-t-il plaidé. Après avoir rappelé la recrudescence des accidents de la route, le procureur Oumar Diallo a estimé qu’il fallait sanctionner les auteurs de ces actes. C’est dans ce sens qu’il a réitéré sa demande, qui consiste à retenir le prévenu Ibrahima Kalil Tounkara dans les liens de la prévention et à le condamner à un (1) an d’emprisonnement et au paiement d’un million de francs guinéens d’amende. Jusque-là libre, le représentant du ministère public a également requis du tribunal qu’il décerne un mandat de dépôt contre le prévenu. C’est dans ce contexte que l’affaire a été mise en délibéré, pour décision être rendue le 17 août 2026. Lébêré Baldé L’article Homicide involontaire : 1 an d’emprisonnement et 1 million de GNF requis contre Ibrahima Kalil Tounkara est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: PTI Centre Mayhem: Suspension, remand deepen storm around Delta Works Commissioner
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi WARRI — The controversy surrounding the alleged assault of the Senior Special Assistant, SSA, on Protocol to the Delta State Government, Mr Simon Mudi, popularly known as Temple, has deepened following indefinite suspension and court remand of the Commissioner for Works (Highway and Urban Roads), Hon Izeze Rume Reuben. The commissioner was suspended Monday by the Delta State Government over alleged links to the July 26 incident at the PTI, Conference Centre, Effurun, Uvwie Local Government Area. The suspension, which took immediate effect, was announced in a statement signed by Secretary to the State Government, SSG, Dr Kingsley Eze Emu. The government said the action was necessary to enable security agencies conduct an unbiased investigation into allegations associating the commissioner with the assault. “The suspension is to enable the Security Agencies carry out an unbiased investigation of allegations associating him with the assault on Temple, at the PTI Center, Effurun, recently,” the statement said. The state government said the decision reflected its commitment to public safety, law and order, insisting that the principle would apply “even when institutions of state are involved.” The development came as an Effurun High Court reportedly ordered the remand of Izeze after he was arraigned by the police in connection with the alleged assault. The court action has added a judicial dimension to the controversy, with the commissioner now facing both administrative suspension and an ongoing criminal proceeding. Reacting to the development, human rights lawyer, Omes Ogedegbe, welcomed the investigation but cautioned against treating the remand order as a conviction. “It would be foolhardy to suggest that the investigation is still being facilitated by the suspension when the investigation had already culminated in a formal criminal charge before the court,” Ogedegbe said. “No individual, irrespective of position, is above the law. However, the law must equally protect every individual accused of an offence.” He said the commissioner was charged in connection with an allegation of attempted murder, stressing that “remand is not a conviction and must never be used as punishment before trial.” Ogedegbe also invoked Section 36(5) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides for the presumption of innocence of a person charged with a criminal offence until proved guilty or the person pleads guilty. He urged the prosecution to justify any continued deprivation of the commissioner’s liberty strictly in accordance with the law. “My position is simple: Investigate where investigation is required. Charge where there is evidence. Prosecute where a case has been established. But do not punish an accused person before conviction,” he said. Ogedegbe further stressed that the suspension was an administrative decision and should not be confused with criminal guilt, just as the remand order did not amount to conviction. “At the end of the day, the rule of law must protect both the victim and the accused. No man is above the law. But equally, no man is beneath the law,” he said. items.title: International Youth Day: PDP mobilises youths to end voter apathy
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) has mobilised its youth structures nationwide ahead of the 2026 International Youth Day, urging greater youth participation in politics as a way of tackling voter apathy and strengthening Nigeria’s democracy. With the celebration holding on Wednesday, August 12, the party has directed its state youth leaders to organise activities in their respective states around the theme: ‘How Youth Political Participation Will Curb Voter Apathy in Nigeria.’ The PDP National Youth Leader, Amb. Ibrahim Bala-Aboki, said the focus was to deepen youth engagement in Nigeria’s democratic process, particularly at a time when voter apathy remains a challenge to effective participation. “The theme underscores the urgent need to deepen youth engagement in Nigeria’s democratic processes, particularly at a time when voter apathy remains a significant challenge to effective democratic participation,” Bala-Aboki said. He said the programme would also provide an opportunity to discuss the role of young Nigerians in the country’s political process. Bala-Aboki said the initiative was in line with the PDP’s emphasis on youth inclusion under its National Chairman, Hon. Abdulrahman Mohammed Takushara. The national youth leader said the party leadership had continued to stress the importance of giving young Nigerians and PDP youths a stake in the affairs of the party. The state-level activities are expected to form part of the nationwide commemoration as the PDP seeks to draw attention to youth participation in democratic governance and national development. “PDP structures across the country are expected to come alive with youth-focused activities as the Party joins the global community in celebrating the strength, creativity and potential of young people,” he said. At the national level, the celebration will hold in Abuja, where party leaders, youth stakeholders, political actors, opinion leaders and other participants are expected to take part. The National Youth Leader also invited other Nigerians to participate in the discussions on expanding youth participation as a means of reducing voter apathy and strengthening Nigeria’s democracy. items.title: AKSA Energy deal: Ghana must conduct own investigations despite US conviction – Osae-Kwapong
items.description: Democracy and Development Fellow at the Ghana Centre for Democratic Development (CDD-Ghana), John Osae-Kwapong, says Ghana must conduct its own investigations into the circumstances surrounding the AKSA Energy deal despite action already taken by authorities in the United States. According to him, the developments surrounding the case raise serious concerns about the integrity of public office and Ghana’s public procurement processes. Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story , Mr Osae-Kwapong acknowledged that authorities in the United States have taken action against the individual at the centre of the case, but argued that this should not end Ghana’s responsibility to examine what happened on its side of the transaction. “Of course we would have to get to, I know on the U.S. side they have dealt with the issue and the individual involved. But I believe that it is also incumbent upon us, as part of our fight against corruption and to ensure integrity in government, that it is incumbent upon us to also further look into this matter,” he said on Monday, August 10. He noted that Ghana has, over the years, committed to strengthening integrity in public office and intensifying the fight against corruption. “So when you read stories like this that allege that the integrity of public office or the integrity of the public procurement process was somehow compromised, then it becomes very worrying,” he explained. Mr Osae-Kwapong said the allegations bring renewed attention to the need for stronger measures to prevent corruption within government and ensure that public procurement processes are conducted transparently. His comments come amid growing calls from civil society organisations and anti-corruption campaigners for Ghanaian authorities to investigate possible local involvement in the alleged bribery scheme. The renewed scrutiny follows the conviction of a former Tema Oil Refinery Managing Director in the United States over bribery-related offences connected to a power plant deal involving Ghana. The development has also raised questions about the circumstances surrounding the renewal of the AKSA Energy agreement with the Ghanaian government in October 2022. Mr Osae-Kwapong stressed that a domestic investigation would be important in establishing whether Ghanaian public officials or institutions breached procurement rules or compromised the integrity of the transaction. He said such an investigation would also demonstrate Ghana’s commitment to accountability and the fight against corruption in public office.

items.title: At least 100 killed after powerful earthquake hits western Colombia
items.description: At least 100 people were killed after a powerful earthquake struck western Colombia early on Monday, knocking down buildings across several cities and injuring at least 87 more, with still others trapped in the rubble. The quake struck just days after Abelardo De La Espriella was sworn in as president, thrusting the new administration into its first major crisis, with memories still fresh of devastating twin earthquakes in neighboring Venezuela in June. The Colombian geological service and its American counterpart, the US Geological Survey, put the magnitude at 7.4. Colombia had initially put it at 6.6. The quake, according to USGS, struck at a depth of 107km near San Jose del Palmar, in Choco, a sparsely populated province on Colombia’s Pacific Coast, but was felt in major cities nationwide. “Significant casualties and damage are likely and the disaster is potentially widespread,” the agency warned. The highest reported death toll was in the western province of Risaralda in Colombia’s coffee-growing region, where Governor Juan Diego Patino, speaking by phone to Caracol Television , reported 42 fatalities. In the province’s capital of Pereira, social media images showed a building with a cracked facade crash to the ground, sending up a dark cloud of dust and debris as onlookers on the street darted away. The impact also toppled one of the towers atop a Gothic-style cathedral in Manizales, and forced nurses in Cali to wheel patients outside in hospital beds, social media and television images showed. Residents and emergency personnel dig through the debris of a partially collapsed building after an earthquake, in Pereira, Colombia on August 10, 2026. — Reuters In Pereira, Mayor Mauricio Salazar said 18 people had died. “The situation is critical,” he told Caracol Radio . In nearby Manizales, Mayor Jorge Eduardo Rojas said three people were killed. One person died in Buenaventura, Colombia’s main Pacific port, when a building collapsed, trapping several people, Mayor Ligia del Carmen Cordoba said. Cali, one of Colombia’s biggest cities, was among the worst hit, though authorities have yet to confirm deaths there. Mayor Alejandro Eder told Caracol at least 30 buildings had collapsed and rescue crews were working at 10 of them. “At this point, two people have already been rescued alive, one elderly woman and one young girl. There are more people trapped,” Eder told Blu Radio earlier. “We have at least 12 critical points and 25 collapsed structures that we are responding to.” He added that the city had asked authorities in Bogota and Medellin to send disaster teams to support rescue efforts. Caracol showed firefighters and Colombian Red Cross workers carrying a survivor on a stretcher from one collapsed building. “The building completely collapsed. It sounded like a bomb. It was horrible,” Juan Carlos Osorio told Caracol Television as he helped remove debris from a collapsed structure in Cali. “All of us neighbors are working together, forming human chains. We need heavy equipment. There are many people trapped.” An elderly woman is carried on furniture near a collapsed building after an earthquake in Cali, Colombia on August 10, 2026. — AFP Colombian officials said they did not fear a tsunami after the early-morning quake, which was also felt in Ecuador, Panama and Venezuela. It prompted building evacuations in Bogota, AFP reporters saw, while news footage showed collapsed buildings elsewhere in the country. The governor of Colombia’s Choco province wrote on X that there were injuries and serious damage to buildings in the department’s capital Quibdo. News outlets aired footage of buildings also destroyed in cities such as Pereira and Manizales in a tourist region called Eje Cafetero. ‘Strong, really strong’ “There is no electricity or cell phone coverage. It was strong, really strong. Things fell in my house,” Martha Estrada, a 66-year-old resident of Eje Cafetero, which means coffee-growing region, told AFP . Alejandro Eder, the mayor of Cali, Colombia’s third largest city, also reported “major damage” that was being evaluated with drones. At least 20 buildings collapsed in the city, with people trapped inside, the mayor said. The city has requested teams from Bogota and Medellin to aid in rescue efforts, he added. People look for survivors amid the rubble of a collapsed building after an earthquake in Cali, Colombia on August 10, 2026. — AFP “The quake was very, very strong,” said Valeria Polo, a 29-year-old content creator in Bogota. Six small airports in western Colombia suspended operations, the civil aeronautics agency said. These airports serve Pereira, Manizales, Quibdo, Armenia, Cartago and Buenaventura, the agency wrote on X. Colombia’s newly inaugurated President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency. “The national government has all of its capabilities deployed to protect lives, assist affected communities and deliver aid wherever it is needed,” he said in a national address around midday from Bogota. “The first priority is rescuing the people trapped under the rubble.” De La Espriella, a right-wing politician who has never before held elected office, earlier said in a video filmed while flying to Bogota that he was suspending his planned activities to lead emergency coordination efforts out of the capital. Bogota Mayor Carlos Galan said on Blu Radio that damage in the national capital appeared to be limited to cracks in the facades of houses and buildings. News outlets aired footage of some buildings with their facades ripped off by the quake. In Bogota some people ran out into the street in their pajamas as emergency sirens rang out, AFP reporters saw. Land of earthquakes and landslides Smaller earthquakes are not uncommon in Colombia, which is crisscrossed by three ranges of the Andean mountains. However, it is landslides which have historically been the deadliest natural disasters in the country, with the Armero disaster in 1985 killing some 25,000 people. Cities in the country’s coffee region, including Armenia and Pereira, suffered a devastating 6.2 magnitude quake in 1999, which killed more than 1,000 people. Twin earthquakes in Venezuela of magnitude 7.2 and 7.5 on June 24 killed more than 6,000 people and caused devastating property damage, mostly on the coast near the capital, Caracas.

items.title: Negotiations with security officials end Warraq residents’ sit-in for better services
items.description: Residents of Warraq Island suspended on Monday a sit-in they had convened, blocking the supply of building materials to a government construction project on the island, to demand access to their own materials and to demand the improvement of basic services, according to residents of the island who spoke to Mada Masr. They said they agreed to suspend the sit-in after negotiations with security officials who promised to accede to their demands. The protest came a week after clashes with security forces resumed over authorities’ restrictions on the delivery of construction materials from the city, part of a policy aimed at emptying the island of its residents to make way for a development project that would turn it into a “new city.” Families living on the Nile island began their sit-in on Sunday outside the arrival point for the ferry that carries vehicles transporting building materials for the government’s construction project on the island. “We’re staying here until the government comes to hear our demands,” one resident told Mada Masr before the sit-in was suspended. “We’re for development, but don’t make things harder for us,” they said, pointing to how residents want to ensure that development does not come at the expense of their lives and daily needs. A second resident said the sit-in had initially been planned to continue until the end of the week, with protestors scheduled to meet on Friday to discuss their next steps. According to the resident, they temporarily suspended the protest after Monday’s negotiations with security officials while they waited for a response to their demands. A third resident summed up the urgent demands as including: the restoration of the work of sewage pumping trucks, as the island’s sewage tanks are full; the removal of the security barriers installed at the island’s two entrances at the Qolaly and Shubra ferry crossings and replacing them with basic inspection procedures; and the repair of street lighting services. Families are also calling for improving healthcare services, according to the third resident, including the provision of a doctor at the island’s hospital. Residents currently have to leave Warraq for emergency and serious medical treatment after the state closed the local health unit in 2021 under the pretext of conducting maintenance. The third resident described these as simple and immediate demands that the state could easily meet as a gesture of “good faith.” Responding to the demands, they said, would be seen as a first step toward engaging with residents, rather than continuing to adopt pressure policies against them and would signal to the residents that the state is prepared to enter into serious talks about conditions under which they can maintain their right to continue living on the island. That would require making everyday life easier, including allowing residents to build and to bring in vehicles carrying construction materials. Another key demand, they said, is for a state representative to engage with residents to discuss their situation and the island’s future. Clashes broke out between security forces and dozens of the island’s residents near the Qolaly ferry crossing last week after a security officer assaulted a boy in an attempt to prevent him from bringing building materials over from the city, according to accounts published online by several residents. The clashes lasted for several consecutive days, with three protestors arrested and later released. The third resident referred to conditions on the island as a “siege” that has lasted for nine years, with heightened security measures such as checkpoints at the island’s entrances, as security forces have shut down three of the five ferries that used to tie the Nile island to the rest of the city. Residents started organizing to oppose the government’s plan to expel them from their homes in 2017 and have continued to do so after the government clarified in the intervening years its plans to develop the island and the issuance of a series of expropriation decisions. Warraq residents have complained of tighter restrictions on the delivery of building materials for around a month, considering the development a form of pressure intended to force them to leave their homes and accept the compensation they are being offered by the government as part of the development project on the island and the expropriation decisions that come with it. Clashes, which flare up periodically on the island between security personnel and residents, have broken out again in recent weeks, as the government has stressed its determination to persist with the New Warraq City project that saw the Housing Ministry handed rights to around 993 out of the island’s 1,295 feddans. Residents have managed to bring the construction materials they need to the island in their own private vehicles or on fishing boats. While security authorities have allowed the entry of materials from time to time, they intensified their checks at the beginning of August, a change that came alongside a shuffle of officials within the Interior Ministry, according to one of the island residents who spoke to Mada Masr. The post Negotiations with security officials end Warraq residents’ sit-in for better services first appeared on Mada Masr .

items.title: PACCI : Elhadj Mamadou Baldé élu vice-président du Conseil exécutif pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest pour 2 ans, présente les opportunités pour la CCIAG
items.description: Élu vice-président du Conseil exécutif de la Chambre panafricaine de commerce et d’industrie (PACCI), représentant de l’Afrique de l’Ouest pour un mandat de deux ans (2026-2028), le président de la Chambre de commerce, d’industrie et d’artisanat de Guinée (CCIAG), Elhadj Mamadou Baldé, accompagné de plusieurs directeurs et conseillers, a animé, ce lundi 10 août, un point de presse à son siège, à Kaloum. Cette rencontre visait à revenir sur son élection, l’importance de cette organisation ainsi que les retombées attendues pour la CCIAG et le secteur privé guinéen. L’élection du président de la CCIAG au Conseil exécutif de la Chambre panafricaine de commerce et d’industrie, une organisation non gouvernementale indépendante créée en 2009 et basée à Addis-Abeba, en Éthiopie, constitue une opportunité majeure pour renforcer la présence de la Guinée et de son secteur privé au sein des réseaux économiques et consulaires africains. Forte de 51 organisations membres issues de 42 pays, la Chambre panafricaine de commerce et d’industrie entend jouer un rôle déterminant en faveur des entreprises guinéennes. Elle contribuera notamment à mieux faire connaître les entreprises et les opportunités d’investissement en Guinée, à développer les relations d’affaires entre opérateurs économiques guinéens et africains, à renforcer la coopération entre les chambres de commerce, à faciliter l’accès des entreprises guinéennes aux marchés africains et à accompagner les acteurs économiques dans la mise en œuvre de la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf), apprend-on. Dans sa communication, Elhadj Mamadou Baldé a d’abord rendu hommage au président de la République ainsi qu’aux membres du Gouvernement pour l’accompagnement constant dont bénéficie le secteur privé. «Le président a cru au secteur privé. Lui et le gouvernement ont accordé une confiance, une approche, un accompagnement au secteur privé guinéen en mettant en place la chambre de commerce d'industrie d'artisanat de Guinée, après 19 ans d’absence». Poursuivant son intervention, le président de la CCIAG est revenu sur les progrès réalisés depuis la relance de l’institution. «Suite à l'avènement du CNRD à la majorité suprême de notre pays, la première action qui a été prise était de mettre en place une chambre de Commerce, d'industrie et d'artisanat de Guinée, une chambre de commerce qui doit jouer son rôle entre l'État et le secteur privé. Aujourd'hui, la chambre de commerce de Guinée a ses quatre années d'activité, mais elle se félicite d'avoir franchi des étapes de réussite pour pouvoir atteindre un certain niveau de représentativité au niveau national, sous-régional et international», a-t-il expliqué. Revenant sur les réformes engagées par l’actuel bureau de la CCIAG, Elhadj Mamadou Baldé a mis en avant les actions entreprises en faveur de la restructuration et du rayonnement de l’institution. «À l'implantation de la chambre de commerce de Guinée, elle a pu réactiver le système de fonctionnement du secteur privé en Guinée, la restructuration des bureaux de représentation dans les régions et dans les préfectures, et la formalisation de plusieurs secteurs dans le domaine du secteur privé. Elle a pu intégrer toutes les institutions consuaires dans le monde, en commençant par la FEWASI (Fédération Ouest Africaine des Chambres de Commerce). Elle a pu intégrer la chambre islamique de commerce, auquel elle est aujourd'hui membre du conseil d'administration de la chambre islamique. Elle a pu intégrer le CPCCAF (conférence permanente des chambres francophones et africaines). Elle a pu intégrer les autres institutions, toutes les institutions liées aux missions du secteur privé entre le privé et l'État. Elle se félicite de pouvoir installer sa représentation à l'international. Son premier bureau consulaire est installé aux États-Unis, il y a près d'un an aujourd'hui. Nous avons été très heureux d'être appuyés et accompagnés par le gouvernement». Revenant sur son élection au Conseil exécutif de la PACCI en qualité de vice-président représentant l’Afrique de l’Ouest, Elhadj Mamadou Baldé a expliqué le déroulement du scrutin. «Trois (3) candidatures ont été retenues par le bureau central, le bureau de la PACCI. Et les autres zones d'Afrique, comme l'Afrique centrale, l'Afrique de l'Est, l'Afrique du Nord, ont tous aussi présenté leurs candidats. Les élections se sont passées en ligne auxquelles chaque président d'une chambre de commerce d'un pays ouvre son lien, il choisit le candidat qu'il préfère. Donc l'Assemblée générale s'est tenue au Maroc à Fès devant l'ensemble de tous les pays africains et élargie aussi à la Banque mondiale, élargie à l'Assemblée internationale de commerce et élargie à d'autres structures à travers le monde. Au résultat de cette élection, la chambre de commerce de Guinée était très heureuse d'être victorieuse à cette élection à 77% de voix pour être élue président pour la sous-région ouest africaine». Très satisfait de cette élection, le président de la CCIAG a estimé que cette distinction dépasse sa personne et constitue une reconnaissance pour l’ensemble du secteur privé guinéen. «Cet acquis c'est l'acquis de tous les secteurs privés guinéens, c'est l'acquis de la chambre de commerce qui rend hommage au président Mamadi Doumbouya grâce à l'appui du gouvernement et à la confiance que le gouvernement accorde à la chambre de commerce, nous avons pu décrocher ce prestigieux poste de responsabilité pour un mandat de deux ans au sein de tous les pays de l'Afrique de l'Est», a-t-il déclaré. Il convient de rappeler que cette organisation, forte de 17 années d’existence, œuvre notamment à la promotion du commerce et des investissements intra-africains, au renforcement de la coopération entre les chambres de commerce, au développement des relations entre les entreprises africaines, au soutien de la participation du secteur privé au processus d’intégration économique du continent ainsi qu’à l’accompagnement de la mise en œuvre de la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf). Mamadou Yaya Barry L’article PACCI : Elhadj Mamadou Baldé élu vice-président du Conseil exécutif pour l’Afrique de l’Ouest pour 2 ans, présente les opportunités pour la CCIAG est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Le Maroc et les États-Unis testent des capacités de frappe à longue portée au centre AMTEC
items.description: Le Maroc et les États-Unis ont franchi une nouvelle étape dans leur coopération militaire. Du 3 au 7 août, les Forces armées royales (FAR) et les forces américaines ont conduit la première démonstration de tir réel exploitant les capacités du Centre africain de formation et d’expérimentation multidomaines (AMTEC), une infrastructure appelée à devenir un pôle régional dédié à l’innovation et à l’évaluation de technologies militaires avancées. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre du programme américain d’extension des champs d’essais relevant du secrétaire à l’Armée de terre des États-Unis. Elle avait pour objectif de tester et d’évaluer des capacités de frappe de précision à longue portée dans des conditions opérationnelles proches du réel. Au-delà de l’exercice lui-même, cette démonstration a permis de mettre à l’épreuve des technologies émergentes et de recueillir des données de terrain destinées à soutenir le développement futur des capacités militaires, tout en accélérant l’intégration de nouveaux systèmes au sein des forces conjointes. Pour le colonel Zouhair Al-Hamdani, officier de coordination des Forces armées royales, l’ambition est de faire du centre AMTEC « un centre régional pour l’innovation, la coopération stratégique et le développement industriel », mais également un centre d’excellence consacré à l’expérimentation, à la validation, à l’évaluation et au perfectionnement des technologies avancées. Selon lui, la tenue de cette première démonstration de tir réel constitue une étape déterminante dans la concrétisation de cette vision. Elle contribue également à renforcer le rôle du centre en tant que plateforme de coopération entre les forces armées et les acteurs de l’industrie de défense. Le commandant du Commandement des États-Unis pour l’Afrique (AFRICOM), le général Dagvin Anderson, a, de son côté, souligné l’importance stratégique du partenariat avec le Maroc. Selon lui, cette coopération offre un environnement favorable au renforcement de la préparation opérationnelle des forces américaines et de leurs partenaires africains. Le responsable américain a estimé que l’AMTEC contribue à approfondir la coopération sécuritaire et à stimuler l’innovation, tout en illustrant l’importance de partenariats fondés sur la confiance pour faire face aux défis sécuritaires communs. La démonstration a mobilisé des militaires et des experts marocains et américains, qui ont participé à l’installation d’un site temporaire d’essais sur le terrain et à la réalisation de l’exercice en collaboration avec des ingénieurs et techniciens issus du secteur de l’industrie de défense. Les essais ont notamment porté sur la vérification des systèmes de communication, l’évaluation de la manœuvrabilité des ailes, des châssis et de différents composants de véhicules de transport. Ils ont également permis de collecter des données liées aux conditions météorologiques et aux procédures de ciblage. Les organisateurs soulignent que les informations recueillies au cours de cette activité serviront de base aux expérimentations futures, au développement de nouvelles capacités et à l’amélioration des méthodes d’emploi dans différents environnements opérationnels. Pour le colonel Michael Gachero, chef de la division de liaison régionale (J5) à l’AFRICOM, cette démonstration illustre l’émergence d’une nouvelle approche de l’entraînement multinational. Celle-ci repose sur l’intégration de technologies émergentes aux côtés des forces des pays partenaires dans des conditions opérationnelles réalistes. Le développement progressif de l’AMTEC au Maroc devrait, selon lui, permettre d’élargir les capacités de formation avancée, de renforcer l’interopérabilité entre les partenaires et d’accélérer l’innovation en coopération avec les pays africains et les alliés internationaux. L’exercice a également mis en évidence le rôle que pourrait jouer le centre dans la modernisation des forces conjointes. L’AMTEC entend notamment rapprocher les besoins opérationnels des innovations technologiques et offrir aux industriels de la défense des environnements d’essais difficiles à reproduire sur certains sites d’expérimentation situés aux États-Unis. Le lieutenant-colonel Corbett Baxter, planificateur d’exercices au sein de la force opérationnelle de l’armée américaine pour l’Europe du Sud et l’Afrique (SETAF-AF), a indiqué que l’objectif du centre est de transformer l’innovation en avantage opérationnel concret. Selon lui, cette démonstration a permis d’évaluer rapidement des technologies émergentes aux côtés des partenaires militaires et d’identifier les solutions les plus efficaces dans un délai réduit. Il a également souligné que la réduction du temps séparant les essais de la mise en service opérationnelle devait permettre aux forces d’accéder plus rapidement à de nouvelles capacités. Au cours de l’exercice, les participants ont utilisé un système à faible coût de missiles de croisière à longue portée, conçu pour offrir des capacités de frappe précises et évolutives. Les essais ont permis de recueillir des données sur les performances de ce système dans des conditions opérationnelles réelles. L’implication d’une jeune entreprise américaine spécialisée dans les technologies de défense a également été présentée comme un exemple de coopération entre les besoins exprimés par les forces armées et les innovations développées par le secteur industriel. Pour le sergent-chef Christopher Hack, adjoint au principal planificateur des pays partenaires au sein de la SETAF-AF, cette démonstration a montré qu’il était possible de combiner entraînement, technologie et coopération opérationnelle afin de concevoir des exercices plus réalistes et davantage fondés sur l’exploitation des données. Les informations recueillies lors de chaque démonstration, a-t-il ajouté, contribueront à améliorer la préparation opérationnelle, à perfectionner les futurs exercices et à adapter les méthodes d’entraînement aux exigences d’environnements sécuritaires de plus en plus complexes. Au-delà de l’évaluation de nouvelles capacités militaires, l’exercice a renforcé le positionnement du Maroc comme partenaire majeur dans le domaine de la sécurité régionale. Il a également mis en lumière le rôle croissant de l’AMTEC comme plateforme d’expérimentation multinationale destinée à tester des technologies et des capacités militaires dans des conditions proches du réel. À terme, le centre devrait poursuivre l’élargissement de ses activités au profit des forces américaines et marocaines, mais aussi de leurs alliés, partenaires et industriels de la défense. Les futurs programmes d’essais devraient notamment porter sur les feux à longue portée, les systèmes autonomes, les communications sans fil et les technologies avancées de détection, avec pour objectif d’accélérer la transformation des innovations technologiques en capacités opérationnelles déployables. Le Commandement des États-Unis pour l’Afrique (AFRICOM), qui supervise la coopération militaire américaine avec 53 pays africains, affirme poursuivre à travers ce type d’initiatives son objectif de soutien aux partenaires africains face aux menaces sécuritaires communes, tout en renforçant la préparation opérationnelle et la capacité de réaction des forces engagées dans la région. The post Le Maroc et les États-Unis testent des capacités de frappe à longue portée au centre AMTEC appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Prisons : fin de la fouille à nu des détenus à l’admission
items.description: L’Administration pénitentiaire met fin à la pratique de la fouille à nu des détenus à leur admission dans les établissements pénitentiaires. Une note de service du directeur général de l’Administration pénitentiaire, l’inspecteur Aliou Ciss, rappelle que cette mesure, jugée « humiliante » et « dégradante », porte atteinte à la dignité humaine. La décision s’inscrit dans une volonté de renforcer le respect des droits humains dans les prisons sénégalaises. La fouille demeure toutefois une mesure de sécurité nécessaire pour prévenir l’introduction d’objets ou de produits prohibés dans les établissements pénitentiaires. Elle est encadrée notamment par les articles 135 et 177 du décret n°2001-362 du 4 mai 2001, ainsi que par les Règles Mandela des Nations unies. Désormais, les responsables des établissements pénitentiaires sont invités à désigner un cadre chargé de superviser les opérations de fouille et à aménager des locaux ou box individuels à cet effet. La fouille des nouveaux détenus ne devra être systématique qu’en cas de nécessité et devra être effectuée en leur laissant leur sous-vêtement. La note précise qu’une fouille à nu ne pourra intervenir qu’à titre exceptionnel, en présence d’une « présomption précise d’infraction » ou d’un « risque avéré pour la sécurité », lorsque la palpation avec les sous-vêtements s’avère insuffisante. Le directeur général rappelle également que les fouilles doivent être effectuées avec tact, sans brutalité et dans le respect de la dignité de la personne, par un personnel pénitentiaire du même sexe que le détenu concerné. La mesure prend effet à compter de sa date de signature. Salla GUEYE

items.title: Govt leaves petrol, diesel prices unchanged for Aug 11
items.description: Pakistan fuel prices, 2026 Official ex-depot prices (PKR/litre) — OGRA & Ministry of Energy notifications Petrol (MS-92) Diesel (HSD) Pre-crisis baseline Source: OGRA / Ministry of Energy (Petroleum Division); Dawn.com · "> The government on Monday kept the prices of petrol and high-speed diesel unchanged as Platts prices were not published on August 10. Petrol will continue to be sold at Rs327.62 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs380.86 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD. According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable on August 11. The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March. Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US. The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel. The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends. The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan. Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes. Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators. Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

items.title: KMA orders removal of unauthorized canopies, awnings at shop frontages in Kumasi
items.description: The Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly (KMA) has issued a 14-day ultimatum to all shop owners and occupiers within the metropolis who have erected unauthorized canopies, awnings, and sheds at the frontage of their premises to remove them immediately. In a public notice dated Monday, August 10, 2026, and signed by the Public Relations Unit of KMA, the Assembly said the unauthorized structures obstruct pedestrian movement, encroach on public spaces and road reserves, and impede emergency access. According to KMA, the structures also “create environmental and safety hazards, and detract the orderly development and appearance of the Metropolis.” The Assembly has directed affected persons to voluntarily remove all unauthorized canopies and associated structures from the frontage of their shops and restore the affected areas to their original condition within fourteen (14) days from the date of the notice. “Failure to comply within the stipulated period will compel the Assembly to remove the offending structures without further notice,” the statement warned. KMA further stated that the cost of any forced removal shall be borne by the owners or occupiers of the shops. Offenders may also be liable to prosecution in accordance with applicable laws and regulations governing physical planning and development control. The Assembly is urging all affected persons to cooperate with authorities to ensure “a safe, accessible, clean, and orderly urban environment.” For further information or clarification, shop owners have been directed to contact the Physical Planning Department of KMA during official working hours. The notice comes amid ongoing efforts by KMA to decongest Kumasi’s central business district and improve pedestrian safety and traffic flow in the Garden City.

Confirmer publiquement des négociations avec les États-Unis relèverait de la pure folie. L'approche gagnante repose sur le déni, l'ambiguïté et la patience stratégique. » Ces déclarations font suite à plusieurs jours de négociations entre l’Iran et l’Oman concernant la réouverture du détroit d’Ormuz. Si Washington a continué à déclarer que les pourparlers avec Téhéran se poursuivaient, le régime iranien nie toute discussion avec l’administration américaine. Téhéran avait déjà déclaré qu’un accord avec l’Oman ne garantirait pas la reprise du transit, et plusieurs demandes ont été formulées : dont des réparations de guerre, la levée des sanctions et du blocus américain sur les ports iraniens. Des médias iraniens ont également indiqué que l'Iran entendait restreindre l’accès des navires américains et israéliens, et qu'il exigerait une compensation de la part des pays qu’il considère comme hostiles. Des officiels iraniens ont confirmé poursuivre les négociations avec l’Oman. Araqchi avait toutefois déclaré précédemment que Téhéran excluait pour l’instant toute négociation directe avec les États-Unis, mais a indiqué que les deux parties échangeaient des messages par l’intermédiaire de médiateurs. Durant le week-end, la position de l’Iran concernant le détroit d’Ormuz et ses demandes maximalistes à l’égard des États-Unis ont également été confirmées, avec la nomination de Mohsen Rezaee, ancien commandant de la Garde révolutionnaire islamique connu pour ses positions radicales et sa défense du contrôle iranien sur le détroit d'Ormuz, au poste de secrétaire du Conseil de sécurité مردم چشم انتظار تصمیماتی سنجیده از شورای عالی امنیت ملی هستند », IRNA, 10 août 2026.'> 2 . Dans son nouveau rôle, il devra notamment coordonner les décisions relatives à la guerre et aux négociations. Hier, 9 août, Donald Trump avait déclaré dans un entretien avec Axios qu'il était prêt à laisser la pression économique s'accroître sur l'Iran plutôt que de lancer une nouvelle offensive militaire : « Nous ne menons que des négociations partielles avec eux. items.title: We are chasing Ebola virus – it is ahead of us, WHO warns
items.description: The latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo began at least three months before it was officially declared – meaning the health authorities are still playing catch-up, the World Health Organization (WHO) has warned. More than 1,900 people have died from the virus since that declaration on 15 May, making this the second-worst Ebola outbreak ever. Infection rates are still high, adding to the concern that the authorities are struggling to get to grips with the spread of the disease. The epicentre of this outbreak of the Bundibugyo species of Ebola, is in the east of DR Congo where insecurity has hampered control efforts. There is also no approved vaccine or any recognised therapeutic drugs, making treating Bundibugyo harder. “We are chasing the virus, the virus is ahead of us,” WHO Africa director Dr Mohamed Janabi said at a news conference in the city of Bunia, which is at the heart of this outbreak. He cited research showing that the virus started spreading in February and was initially misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid. Janabi also said that, in part because of insecurity, health workers are only reaching about 30% of the cases with the rest dying at home. Traditional burial practices – where mourners touch the deceased’s body – and a suspicion of health authorities in some communities have also made things difficult. But there are now several dedicated treatment centres in the east of DR Congo and people are getting diagnosed much more quickly. So far there have been 4,294 confirmed cases and 1,960 deaths, DR Congo’s health ministry has said. The largest recorded outbreak was in West Africa between 2014 and 2016 when 11,325 people died.

items.title: Tourism Minister prioritises unfinished cultural centres over promised Kumasi theatre
items.description: The Minister of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts, Abla Dzifa Gomashie has said that the government will prioritise completing existing cultural facilities before starting a new National Theatre in Kumasi. Speaking at the Government Accountability Series on Monday, 10th August 2026, she said a tour of cultural facilities in the Ashanti Region had convinced her that it was prudent to complete existing projects before starting new ones. “I took a tour of Ashanti Region’s theatre and centre for national culture spaces and I have suggested to cabinet that instead of starting a new one, we focus on finishing what has been started and cabinet is in approval of that suggestion. So that is why is going to happen and then if the opportunity comes we start a new one,” she said. The Minister said her proposal to Cabinet was intended to ensure that uncompleted cultural projects initiated by previous governments were completed before work began on the proposed National Theatre in Kumasi. Her comments come a few days after Kumasi-based broadcaster Austine Woode raised concerns about preparations for the construction of a second National Theatre in Kumasi, as promised in the manifesto of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) ahead of the 2024 elections. Speaking during the ninth edition of Joy FM’s Showbiz Roundtable on Saturday, 8th August 2026, Austine expressed disappointment in the minister’s unresponsiveness to initiating the construction of the theatre in their region. “I am from Kumasi, has she spoken to anybody about the land on which they will build the Kumasi theatre? I am a stakeholder there. If she had had any conversation like that, I would know that they are looking for the land. They are not doing it,” he said. Meanwhile, the Centre for National Culture in Kumasi, popularly known as Dwabrem, has for many years been earmarked for renovation by successive governments. The previous government also laid a foundation for an amphitheatre in Kumasi.
