items.title: RDC : des otages détenus par les ADF retrouvent leur communauté sur fond d’intensification des opérations de l’armée congolaise
items.description: Il aura fallu plusieurs mois de captivite et l'offensive de l'armee congolaise pour que les cinq femmes et six hommes retenus en otages par le groupe arme ADF (affilie a Daech) puissent enfin retrouver leur communaute dans l'est de la Republique democratique du Congo (RDC), le 9 août, selon un reportage de Ruptly. Les troupes congolaises multiplient actuellement les operations contre le groupe arme, originaire de l'Ouganda, apres son attaque meurtriere a Banana ecole, survenue le 8 août, qui a coûte la vie a 13 civils congolais. Enlevee alors qu'elle travaillait dans son champ Face a la camera, l'ancienne otage Masika Muhasa Feza a declare qu'elle avait ete enlevee par les combattants de l'ADF a Sabasaba, alors qu'elle travaillait dans son champ. Elle a ete forcee de transporter le butin du groupe arme avec la promesse d'etre liberee apres la traversee du fleuve Ituri. « Mais nous avons continue a marcher pendant plusieurs jours sans nous arreter », a-t-elle deplore. L'enfant de Masika Muhasa Feza, qui avait egalement ete enleve, a ete garde en otage dans la brousse, declare sa mere, avant d'ajouter : « ils nous ont dit que les enfants seraient liberes une fois leur formation islamique terminee ». « C'est deja une benediction d'aller aux champs et d'en revenir vivants » Catherine Amabunyambya, une autre habitante de la region, a indique que la crainte des attaques des rebelles de l'ADF instille la peur de se rendre aux champs pour travailler : « C'est deja une benediction d'aller aux champs et d'en revenir vivants », a-t-elle affirme. « Nous souffrons car ils enlevent nos enfants, et nous ignorons s'ils sont encore en vie ou morts. C'est dechirant de perdre un enfant dans de telles circonstances », a-t-elle confie. Adressant un cri de detresse aux autorites, Catherine Amabunyambya a deplore un village « presque desert a cause des attaques rebelles », indiquant que les habitants, contraints a la fuite, « vivent dans d'extremes difficultes ». Appelant le gouvernement a instaurer la paix pour que les habitants puissent retrouver leur village et leur vie d'avant, elle a conclu son temoignage par cette note d'espoir : « Toute guerre a une fin ». Il convient de noter que le conflit meurtrier dans l'est de la RDC, qui se poursuit depuis des annees, est a l'origine de centaines de prises d'otage, de dizaines de milliers de tues et de millions de deplaces. Selon le Haut-Commissariat des Nations Unies pour les refugies (HCR), les personnes deplacees dans cette region pourraient atteindre 9 millions d'ici fin 2026, dans une region tres riche en minerais strategiques.

items.title: France : un refus de visa finalement annulé après recours à Nantes
items.description: Un refus de visa long séjour du consulat de France en Tunisie à une ressortissante tunisienne a finalement été remis en cause par la Commission de recours contre les décisions de refus de visa d’entrée en France (CRRV). Une ressortissante tunisienne avait demandé un visa de long séjour sous le statut « visiteur », mais sa demande a été rejetée, selon son avocat, Me Fayçal Megherbi, qui a ensuite saisi la CRRV, à Nantes, pour contester la réponse défavorable. « Comme c’est fréquemment le cas dans la pratique contentieuse de l’immigration, les motifs d’un tel refus reposent souvent sur des appréciations stéréotypées ou insuffisamment étayées concernant les garanties de retour ou le niveau de ressources », explique Me Meghrebi, avocat au Barreau de Paris, spécialiste du droit des étrangers. Un refus de visa peut être contesté à Nantes, assure Me Megherbi Après l’examen du recours, les autorités françaises ont finalement donné une suite favorable à la demande. « À l’issue de l’examen de cette requête, j’ai décidé de donner une suite favorable à cette demande de visa. Les autorités consulaires françaises à Tunis contacteront prochainement la requérante pour délivrer le visa de long séjour sollicité », a tranché le sous-directeur des visas à Nantes. La requérante doit donc être prochainement contactée par le consulat français à Tunis pour la délivrance de son visa, selon l’avocat, en soulignant que cette issue favorable signifie qu’une décision consulaire peut être contestée. La CRRV constitue ainsi une voie permettant de remettre en cause une décision défavorable auprès des autorités françaises. L’article France : un refus de visa finalement annulé après recours à Nantes est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Running for an office and running the office
items.description: Reflections Ahead of Nigeria’s 2027 General Elections Running for office is not the same as running the office Nigeria is gradually entering another election season. Soon, the familiar rituals will intensify. There will be defections, coalitions, declarations, endorsements, rallies, manifestos and carefully choreographed appearances. Politicians will rediscover marketplaces and neglected communities. Candidates who have rarely interacted with ordinary citizens will suddenly speak the language of the street. Amid this familiar political theatre, Nigerians should ask a more consequential question. Are we choosing people who know how to run for office, or people who know how to run the office? The distinction is fundamental. Running for office requires political machinery, money, networks, visibility, messaging, party structures, coalition-building and an ability to mobilise voters. Running the office requires judgement, competence, discipline, integrity, policy knowledge, the ability to build teams, manage institutions, make difficult choices and accept responsibility for consequences. The skills that get a candidate elected are not necessarily the skills that enable a leader to govern effectively. Nigeria has too often discovered this distinction only after elections have been won and governments have been formed. The campaign is not the job Our political culture has become remarkably sophisticated at evaluating campaigns and surprisingly weak at interrogating governing capacity. We frequently ask whether a candidate can win, but we devote far less attention to whether that candidate can govern. We debate where candidates come from, the size of their political structures, their endorsements, religion, ethnicity, zoning and electoral arithmetic. These considerations may matter politically, but none guarantees competence in office. A candidate can understand the mathematics of winning elections and still have little understanding of economics, public administration, national security or institutional reform. A politician may know how to assemble a winning coalition without knowing how to assemble a competent cabinet. Nigerians should therefore examine not only the ability of candidates to secure power, but also their preparedness to exercise it responsibly. Nigeria cannot afford another apprenticeship in government The stakes in 2027 will be unusually high. Nigeria faces profound economic pressures, insecurity, unemployment and underemployment, institutional fragility, declining public trust and growing frustration among young people. The country also operates in an increasingly uncertain international environment in which geopolitics, technology, climate pressures and changing global economic relationships demand sophisticated leadership. This is not an environment in which leaders should begin learning the job after winning it. Nigeria cannot continue electing people first and discovering their governing philosophy later. We cannot keep handing enormous public responsibilities to politicians whose principal qualification is that they have mastered the internal politics of their parties or assembled sufficient resources to win an election. The presidency is not an internship, a governorship is not an apprenticeship, and a ministerial appointment should not be treated as political compensation. Public office is a responsibility to manage complex institutions affecting millions of lives. Competence must therefore become a democratic demand. Interrogate the record, not the rhetoric As 2027 approaches, voters should become considerably more demanding. Every serious candidate should be required to demonstrate what he or she has managed before and what became better as a result. Where candidates have previously held public office, Nigerians should examine their records rather than the mythology surrounding them. Voters should consider what happened to public finances, whether institutions were strengthened, whether services improved, whether competent people were appointed, how criticism was handled and whether public resources were treated as genuinely public. Candidates from the private sector, civil society or other professions should face the same scrutiny. Their institutional record, difficult decisions, leadership choices and ability to translate ideas into outcomes should be examined. Leadership should leave evidence, and political biographies filled with positions but lacking measurable achievements should not be enough to earn public trust. Look at the people around the candidate Nigerians should also pay closer attention to the people surrounding those who seek power. No president or governor governs alone. The quality of leadership is often revealed before an election by the quality of people a candidate attracts, trusts and listens to. A politician surrounded exclusively by praise singers should concern voters. A candidate unable to tolerate disagreement before acquiring power is unlikely to suddenly embrace dissent after acquiring it. The advisers, political associates and individuals entrusted with responsibility during a campaign can provide an early indication of the governing culture that may follow. Competence and character should matter at least as much as political loyalty. Manifestos should become governing documents Nigeria must also rethink the role of manifestos. Too often, manifestos are treated as campaign accessories. They are launched ceremonially, quoted selectively and quietly forgotten after elections. In 2027, voters, journalists, universities, professional associations and civil society should interrogate manifestos as prospective governing contracts. Promises to create jobs should explain which sectors will generate them. Security proposals should identify what will change. Poverty reduction commitments should indicate the policies, resources and realistic timelines involved. Proposals for restructuring or institutional reform should explain which laws and institutions must change and how the necessary political coalitions will be built. The objective is not to expect politicians to predict the future perfectly. Governing inevitably encounters unexpected events. The objective is to establish whether candidates have thought seriously about the country they seek to govern and whether their promises can survive contact with governing realities. Citizens are not spectators There is also a deeper democratic problem. Election seasons encourage citizens to behave like supporters rather than employers. We defend candidates, attack their opponents, wear political colours and repeat slogans. Legitimate questions about competence are sometimes interpreted as attacks on preferred candidates. Democracy requires something more demanding. Politicians seeking public office are asking citizens to entrust them with responsibility, resources and authority. Voters should therefore approach elections with the seriousness of employers assessing applicants for exceptionally consequential jobs. No serious institution hires someone simply because the applicant is popular, wealthy, charismatic, comes from a particular community or can defeat other applicants. It asks whether the person can actually perform the job. The standards for managing a country of more than 200 million people should certainly not be lower. Political loyalty should never require intellectual surrender. Citizens can support candidates and still ask difficult questions. Indeed, responsible democratic participation requires precisely that level of scrutiny. 2027 must be an election about governing Nigeria’s 2027 elections will inevitably involve personalities, parties, regions, alliances and political calculations. That is the nature of competitive politics. Beneath all of this, however, should be a more important national test: which candidates are actually prepared to govern? The answer cannot be determined by the best speech, the loudest supporters, dominance of social media, the largest campaign war chest or even the ability to win an election. Nigeria needs leaders capable of translating political authority into public value. As aspirants begin positioning themselves and campaigns gather momentum, Nigerians should imagine not only the candidate on a campaign stage surrounded by supporters and making promises, but also the same person in office after inauguration, confronted by difficult decisions affecting millions of lives. At that point the campaign crowd will be gone, the music will have stopped, the slogans will offer little assistance, and the cameras will have moved elsewhere. What will remain are judgement, competence, character and leadership. In 2027, Nigerians should not merely decide who can run for office. They should decide who can run the office.

items.title: Drowning in data, dying from bad decisions -BigData Ghana CEO charges Africa to act
items.description: When the Department of Geomatic Engineering at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology marked its 50th anniversary on Friday, it brought together alumni, partners, and the next generation of engineers to reflect on a journey that began with two students and a mandate to map Ghana. The speaker it invited did not come to merely celebrate. Prof. Samuel Andam-Akorful, Head of Department, had been clear in his opening remarks about where the department’s eyes were fixed. “We are preparing ourselves to be a very modern department that trains the best geospatial professionals you can find wherever you are,” he said. “The next fifty years will be defined by what we build from here.” Mr. Baffoe, Managing Director and Co-Founder of BigData Ghana Limited, took the floor with a single argument. Ghana, he told the assembled engineers, academics, students, and executives, does not lack data. What it lacks is the will and the infrastructure to act on it. “Africa does not only have a data problem,” he said. “Africa has a decision problem.” His argument was straightforward. The continent has accumulated more data than at any previous point in its history. Satellite imagery. Climate records. Agricultural surveys. Census data. Mobile network information stretching back decades. None of it, he said, is in short supply. What is in short supply is the institutional will and the technical infrastructure to convert it into decisions that change outcomes. The timing was pointed. In recent weeks, flooding has displaced families across Accra and shut down commercial activity in some of the city’s busiest areas. The spatial risk data for those corridors, Mr. Baffoe noted, has been available for years. What was missing was not the information. It was the system that should have acted on it. Mr. Baffoe has spent eight years building that system. BigData Ghana is an AWS Certified Partner and was selected as the only Ghanaian Earth Observation company among ten African organisations chosen for the EU-AU Space Partnership Programme. Its work is live, not in development. He described three deployments. The first is the Ghana Agricultural Information and Monitoring System, which uses satellite imagery and vegetation data to make farming activity visible to banks and investors who have historically declined to lend because they could not verify what was in the ground or where. In 2021, the work behind the system won BigData Ghana the Digital Earth Africa Innovation Challenge, making it the first Ghanaian company to take the continent-wide competition. The second is the National Forest Monitoring System, which tracks changes across Ghana’s forest landscape in near real time. Alongside it runs ForestTrace AI, a deforestation tracking platform that draws on historical data, monitors present conditions, and predicts where deforestation is likely to occur next. Its scope extends beyond human settlement expansion to include bush fires, illegal mining, and every other driver of forest loss. The system is now being developed toward EU Deforestation Regulation compliance, helping cocoa farmers and gold producers demonstrate that their supply chains are free of deforestation risk, a requirement that is reshaping how Ghanaian commodities access international markets. ForestTrace AI was built during and won the Gen AI for Geospatial Challenge hosted by AWS, Women+ in Geospatial, 5G, and Lunate AI, with the result announced in January 2026. The two systems together allow institutions to intervene early rather than respond late, which is, Mr. Baffoe argued, the only intervention that works. The third is a Flood Intelligence Agent in development that will allow government agencies, district assemblies, and emergency services to query spatial data and receive specific guidance rather than static maps. He offered an example of what that looks like in practice. “Imagine a district assembly asking an AI agent: what are the flood implications of this proposed development, and receiving an evidence-based assessment in minutes,” he said. “Imagine emergency agencies identifying which communities need the earliest warnings before the rain arrives.” The private sector, he said, is not exempt from the same failure. Banks pricing risk on property portfolios without spatial data are, in his words, pricing blind. Developers approving sites without flood exposure assessments are carrying liabilities their boards have not fully considered. The intelligence that would change those decisions, he said, already exists. The lecture’s sharpest passage came when Mr. Baffoe turned from what has been built to what has not lasted. He told the room that Africa produces pilot projects with impressive regularity. Platforms are launched. Dashboards are demonstrated. Awards are collected. Then, in most cases, the funding ends and the systems are quietly set aside. “How many of these systems become part of how institutions operate every day?” he asked. “How many survive after funding ends? How many produce measurable change?” He called for a shift in how the profession defines success. Not the technical sophistication of what is built, but the evidence that something changed because it was built. A farmer who received financing. A forest that was protected. A community that received a warning in time. To the students in the room he was direct. Learn to code, he said. Python, SQL, cloud computing, artificial intelligence. Not because every engineer must become a software developer, but because the scope of what you can influence is determined by what you can build. Then start with a different question. “Do not begin with: what map can I create,” he said. “Begin with: what decision must improve.” He ended by addressing the assumption, common among young professionals across the continent, that world-class technology cannot be built from within Africa. “A team in Ghana can use African data, global cloud infrastructure, open-source tools and local knowledge to build solutions of international quality,” he said. “The opportunity is here. What we need is the courage to build.” The Department of Geomatic Engineering at KNUST was founded in 1976. Friday’s lecture was the first in a series the department intends to hold annually. The second speaker at the event was Krijn Driessen, Project Manager of the WaterWorX Project at VEI Ghana. About BigData Ghana Limited Your most expensive decisions deserve better intelligence. BigData Ghana is a technology company that leverages geospatial intelligence to help organisations plan, develop, invest, and execute with confidence. Headquartered in Accra, the company serves government institutions, banks, investors, private sector businesses, agricultural enterprises, logistics operators, and infrastructure developers across Ghana and the wider African continent. An AWS Certified Partner, BigData Ghana was selected as the only Ghanaian Earth Observation company among ten African organisations for the EU-AU Space Partnership Programme. In 2021, it became the first Ghanaian company to win the Digital Earth Africa Innovation Challenge. Its work spans geospatial intelligence, cloud computing, data analytics, and business intelligence. Eight years of Ghana-specific spatial data. Fifty-plus projects delivered. You Decide Better With Us.

items.title: Canicule en Europe : la vague de chaleur pourrait coûter 180 milliards d'euros et annuler la croissance de l'UE
items.description: La canicule et la secheresse extremes qui ont touche une grande partie de l'Europe cet ete pourraient reduire a neant la croissance economique attendue de l'Union europeenne en 2026, a rapporte le 10 août Der Spiegel , en se referant a une etude de la banque neerlandaise Triodos, specialisee dans le financement de projets durables. Selon ce rapport, les perturbations economiques provoquees par la canicule pourraient reduire le produit interieur brut (PIB) de l'Union europeenne d'environ 1 %, ce qui equivaut a des pertes d'environ 180 milliards d'euros. La principale cause invoquee est la baisse de la productivite du travail : selon les estimations, ce facteur a lui seul pourrait reduire le PIB de l'UE de 0,6 %. Les repercussions s'etendent toutefois bien au-dela du marche du travail. L'agriculture serait particulierement touchee : selon les previsions de la banque, la production y chuterait de 3 a 7 %. De plus, d'apres Der Spiegel , les consequences de la canicule sont aggravees par la hausse des prix des denrees alimentaires, les restrictions en matiere de production d'electricite et l'augmentation des tarifs de l'electricite, ainsi que par les perturbations dans le fonctionnement des transports routiers, ferroviaires et fluviaux. Selon les estimations de Triodos, la France pourrait subir les dommages les plus importants : la canicule pourrait reduire son PIB d'environ 1,4 % et entraîner une contraction de l'economie dans son ensemble de 0,6 %. Des pertes importantes sont egalement prevues pour l'Italie, l'Espagne et la Belgique. Aux Pays-Bas, les consequences pourraient reduire a neant la croissance economique attendue cette annee. Les pays qui ont connu des periodes plus courtes de chaleur anormale, comme la Pologne, seraient moins touches. Selon les donnees du service climatique europeen Copernicus, les deux premiers mois de l'ete 2026 ont ete les plus chauds jamais enregistres en Europe occidentale, la temperature moyenne en juin-juillet ayant depasse la norme climatique de pres de trois degres. Le 8 août, le president du principal syndicat agricole francais, Arnaud Rousseau, a evoque une catastrophe climatique « d'une ampleur que nous n'avons jamais vue en agriculture sur une telle duree ». a cet egard, il a appele l'etat a apporter un « soutien massif ». Outre les problemes rencontres dans le secteur agricole, plusieurs pays europeens ont ete touches par des incendies de foret d'une ampleur sans precedent, provoques par une chaleur et une secheresse exceptionnelles. Rien qu'en France, la superficie des terres ravagees par les flammes depasse les 115 000 hectares. Selon les donnees du Financial Times debut août, la catastrophe naturelle qui s'est abattue sur plusieurs pays europeens a deja cause des dommages economiques estimes a 3,1 milliards d'euros , ce montant ne refletant qu'une partie des coûts totaux, qui devraient continuer a augmenter.

items.title: “It’s time for us to make our voices heard” – GAUA on strike over allowance disparity
items.description: The Ghana Association of University Administrators (GAUA) says it has been compelled to embark on industrial action after years of what it describes as unfair disparities in allowances between teaching and non-teaching staff in public universities. The Association began an indefinite strike on Monday, August 10, 2026, directing its members to withdraw their services until their concerns over remuneration and other conditions of service are addressed. Speaking in an interview on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Monday, August 10, GAUA General Secretary, Charles Kojo Aidoo, said the association has historically avoided industrial action but believes the current situation requires its members to take a stronger position. “GAUA has not gone on strike for so many years. They don’t go on strike, but we believe that this is the time for us to make our voice heard. And we are being taken for granted for far too long,” he said. Mr Aidoo cited disparities in market premiums between teaching and non-teaching staff as one of the major concerns behind the strike. He said an assistant lecturer, who may be newly employed and still on probation, receives a market premium of about GH¢7,400, while the registrar of a university receives approximately GH¢6,000. He added that the director of finance of a university also receives a market premium of about GH¢6,000. “The person takes much more market premium than the registrar and director of finance of the university. And we believe that this is unfair,” he said. Mr Aidoo said the disparity between teaching and non-teaching staff has become increasingly wide and could eventually affect the ability of universities to attract and retain professionals. He argued that remuneration should reflect the responsibilities, skills, experience and qualifications attached to each position. The GAUA General Secretary stressed that the association’s concerns should not be interpreted as an attempt to compete with the University Teachers Association of Ghana (UTAG). “It is not about UTAG. UTAG has negotiated for their market premium. We are also saying that. They are also part of the architecture of the university. We are professionals doing our work in the university. Our work should also be valued.” He said professional staff within universities, including accountants, architects and other specialists, are required to possess relevant professional qualifications in addition to their academic credentials. Mr Aidoo explained that an accountant working in a university, for instance, is expected to be professionally qualified, while architects are required to meet professional standards before they can undertake certain responsibilities. He therefore believes their remuneration should adequately reflect their professional expertise and responsibilities. GAUA says the widening disparity could have implications for staff retention, particularly if experienced professionals continue to feel undervalued compared with other categories of university employees. Mr Aidoo warned that failure to address the situation could eventually result in a shortage of experienced professional staff within public universities. He maintained that the association is not demanding preferential treatment but is seeking a remuneration structure that appropriately reflects the responsibilities and professional competencies of its members. The association is therefore calling for urgent engagement with the relevant authorities to review the allowance structure and address what it considers to be longstanding inequities. GAUA says it remains prepared to engage stakeholders to resolve the dispute but insists that its members’ concerns can no longer be ignored.

items.title: Ghana’s graduates trapped in unemployment as the system fails to absorb them
items.description: Every year, thousands of young people graduate from universities, colleges and other tertiary institutions across Ghana. They spend years studying, writing examinations and preparing for what they believe will be the next stage of their lives: getting a job and building a career. But for many graduates, the journey from the classroom to the workplace has become a frustrating struggle. After years of education, many find themselves at home, sending out applications, attending interviews and waiting for opportunities that seem increasingly difficult to find. Some spend months or even years searching for work. Others are forced to accept jobs unrelated to their qualifications, while some eventually give up on their career aspirations altogether. This is not simply an individual problem. It is a national problem. The Ghana Statistical Service has consistently highlighted the difficult employment situation facing young people in the country. Its labour force reports show that young people make up a significant share of those without work. Behind these statistics, however, are real people: graduates with ambitions, families that sacrificed to educate them, and young Ghanaians who simply want an opportunity to work and contribute to society. When Education and Employment Do Not Connect One of the biggest problems is the gap between what many students are taught in school and what the workplace actually demands. Too often, education remains heavily focused on theory. Students read textbooks, attend lectures, write examinations and graduate with certificates, but many leave school without enough practical experience. The workplace, however, demands more. Employers want people who can communicate effectively, use technology, prepare reports, solve problems, work in teams and adapt quickly. They want graduates who can contribute from the beginning. This creates a difficult situation. A graduate may have the required academic qualification but still be told that they lack the practical skills needed for the job. The problem becomes even more frustrating when employers demand two or more years of experience for entry-level positions. How is a fresh graduate supposed to gain experience if nobody is willing to give them their first opportunity? This is where universities and other tertiary institutions must take a serious look at what they are offering students. Education should not end with a certificate. Students should leave school with skills they can actually use. Universities need stronger partnerships with industries. Internships, apprenticeships, practical projects and workplace exposure should become a more important part of tertiary education. In a world increasingly driven by technology, education must also keep pace with the changing nature of work. There Are Simply Not Enough Jobs Even when graduates have the right skills, another problem remains: there are simply not enough jobs. Government, which has traditionally been one of the biggest employers of graduates, cannot absorb everyone entering the labour market. Budget constraints and economic pressures have made public-sector employment increasingly limited. The private sector, meanwhile, is not creating jobs quickly enough to absorb the growing number of young people entering the workforce. The result is intense competition. One job advertisement can attract hundreds of applications. A single vacancy can receive applications from people with degrees, professional qualifications, internships and years of experience. For a young graduate, it can feel as though the competition is almost impossible to win. But there is another issue that cannot be ignored: the perception that connections matter more than qualifications. In Ghana, many young people believe that knowing the right person can sometimes matter more than having the right credentials. There are also concerns about vacancies that are not openly advertised and positions that are filled through personal networks. Whether every such claim is accurate or not, the perception itself is damaging. A young person should not have to know someone in an organisation to have a fair chance of getting a job. Recruitment must be transparent, competitive and based on merit. “Start a Business” Is Not a Complete Solution Whenever unemployment is discussed, one common response is: “Start your own business.” Entrepreneurship is important, and initiatives such as YouStart are intended to help young people establish businesses and create employment. But starting a business is not as simple as having an idea. A graduate may have a good business plan but no money to execute it. Banks often require collateral that many young people do not have. Access to government funding and other support can also be difficult and, in some cases, slow. We cannot tell young people to become entrepreneurs while leaving them without the resources needed to make entrepreneurship possible. Business training, affordable financing, mentorship, market access and simplified support systems are all necessary. Entrepreneurship should certainly be part of the solution, but it cannot become an excuse for failing to create enough formal employment opportunities. What Needs to Change? Ghana cannot solve graduate unemployment by simply producing more graduates and hoping the economy will absorb them. The country needs a deliberate strategy. First, education must become more practical. Universities and other tertiary institutions should work closely with industries to understand the skills employers need. Students should have more opportunities to gain practical experience before they graduate. Second, Ghana must create more jobs. Government investment should focus on sectors with the potential to employ large numbers of young people, including manufacturing, agriculture, technology and small and medium-sized businesses. Third, companies must give young people a chance. Not every graduate can have years of experience. Businesses should create genuine entry-level opportunities, internships and graduate trainee programmes that allow young people to develop professionally. Finally, recruitment must be fair and transparent. Vacancies should be openly advertised, selection processes should be clear, and qualifications and competence should matter. Ghana Cannot Afford to Waste Its Young People Graduate unemployment is more than an economic problem. It is a waste of human potential. Every unemployed graduate represents skills that are not being fully used, ideas that may never be developed and potential contributions to national development that are being lost. Ghana has invested heavily in educating its young people. The country cannot afford to educate them and then leave them stranded at the point where their education is supposed to become productive. Young Ghanaians are not asking for everything to be handed to them. Many are asking for something much simpler: a fair opportunity. They want a chance to prove themselves, gain experience, earn a living and build a future. The solution will require more than speeches and short-term programmes. Ghana must reform how it prepares young people for work, expand opportunities for employment, support genuine entrepreneurship and ensure that recruitment is based on merit. The country’s graduates are ready. The question is whether Ghana is ready to create the opportunities to absorb them.

items.title: SDA leads partnership with government to complete Agenda 111 projects
items.description: The Ghana Adventist Health Services of the Seventh-day Adventist (SDA) Church has expressed its commitment to partner the government to complete some Agenda 111 hospital projects across the country. The commitment was made when a delegation from the Ghana Adventist Health Services, led by Dr James Antwi, paid a courtesy call on the Minister for Health, Kwabena Mintah Akandoh, as part of efforts to deepen collaboration between faith-based health institutions and the government. During the meeting, the SDA delegation presented a proposal outlining four key areas in which it hopes to support healthcare delivery. These include trauma care, holistic wellness, oncology and cancer treatment, as well as rehabilitation and other health services. The proposal seeks to position the SDA Church as a strategic partner in strengthening healthcare delivery, particularly in underserved communities where access to quality medical services remains a challenge. The engagement also focused on the completion and operationalisation of some of the health facilities under the government’s Agenda 111 programme. Mr Akandoh stressed the importance of partnerships in meeting the country’s growing healthcare needs, saying government alone could not shoulder the responsibility of providing all the infrastructure and services required by the sector. He called on faith-based organisations, including the Christian Health Association of Ghana (CHAG), as well as private sector institutions, to support efforts to complete and operationalise the unfinished Agenda 111 facilities. The minister commended the SDA Church for its longstanding contribution to healthcare delivery, particularly in deprived and underserved communities, and welcomed its willingness to work with the government. He assured potential partners that the government was prepared to provide the necessary guidance to organisations interested in supporting the completion of Agenda 111 projects. According to the minister, such partnerships would not require partners to make financial contributions directly to government. Instead, organisations would be expected to provide direct support towards the completion of selected projects. He encouraged CHAG and private sector players to identify specific Agenda 111 facilities or areas where they would like to contribute, with the government providing the necessary direction to facilitate the projects. The meeting also provided an opportunity for the minister to outline broader plans to expand healthcare infrastructure and improve access to specialised medical services across the country. Mr Akandoh reiterated his position that doctors must accept postings to designated areas as part of efforts to ensure a more equitable distribution of health professionals nationwide. He also disclosed plans by the government to construct six regional hospitals in the newly created regions. According to him, funding has been provided for the construction of three of the six hospitals in 2026, while work on the remaining three is expected to begin in 2027. The minister further announced plans to expand access to specialised cardiac care through the construction of two cardiology centres, one in Tamale and another at the Komfo Anokye Teaching Hospital in Kumasi. He also disclosed that the cardiac catheterisation laboratory, commonly known as a Cath Lab, at the Korle Bu Teaching Hospital had recently been installed and commissioned by the President. The facility is expected to strengthen the hospital’s capacity to diagnose and treat patients requiring specialised cardiac procedures. Mr Akandoh also highlighted three major interventions being pursued by the government as part of efforts to improve access to healthcare and move Ghana towards Universal Health Coverage by 2030. These are the Free Primary Healthcare initiative, the uncapping of the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS), and the establishment of the Ghana Medical Care Trust Fund. The minister said the interventions formed part of broader efforts to remove barriers to healthcare access and improve the quality and availability of medical services. The engagement between the SDA Ghana Adventist Health Services and the Ministry of Health comes as the government seeks greater involvement from faith-based organisations and private sector players in addressing gaps in the country’s health infrastructure. With its long history of providing healthcare services, particularly in communities with limited access to medical facilities, the SDA Church’s proposed partnership could provide additional support towards completing and bringing some Agenda 111 facilities into operation. The meeting therefore marks a further step towards strengthening collaboration between government and faith-based health institutions, with both sides seeking to improve access to quality and affordable healthcare for communities across Ghana.

items.title: Hamamat launches competition series with GH¢10,000 grand prize
items.description: Ghanaian wellness and cultural experience brand Hamamat has launched a new competition series, offering participants the chance to win a GH¢10,000 cash prize. The competition series, which runs from August to December, will feature a number of challenges based on popular Ghanaian foods, games and cultural activities. The challenges include ice cream eating, pepper eating, Ampe, Oware, suya and kebab eating, Jollof, ice block eating and other surprise competitions to be announced. The first challenge, an ice cream and popsicle eating competition, was held at the Hamamat Wellness House in Accra over the weekend. The event brought contestants together for an afternoon of competition, music and entertainment as participants battled to prove their endurance in the opening challenge. The series is designed to give participants the opportunity to compete in individual challenges, qualify and work their way towards the GH¢10,000 grand prize. According to the organisers, the concept is to transform familiar Ghanaian foods, games and cultural experiences into live entertainment that people can participate in and share. Participants aged 16 years and above can take part, depending on the specific challenge. Those below 18 will require parental or guardian consent, while some competitions may be restricted to adults for safety reasons. Competition rules and eligibility requirements will be announced for each challenge. Interested participants are expected to follow Hamamat on social media for announcements and registration details. The competition series forms part of Hamamat’s broader focus on promoting Ghanaian culture and traditional experiences through its wellness and lifestyle brand. Its experiences include the Shea Butter Museum, which showcases the history and culture of shea, and the Hamamat Wellness House, an African-inspired wellness and experience space in Accra. The competition series seeks to build on these experiences by turning familiar activities such as eating, playing and traditional games into interactive entertainment. The organisers are encouraging people to nominate friends and family members who they believe have the skills or endurance to take on the various challenges as the series continues through December.

items.title: New investigation team initiates formal proceedings into Mir Raza Ali murder
items.description: A new investigation team formed by the Sindh IGP on Monday initiated formal proceedings into the murder of business owner Mir Raza Ali, following the findings of a second post-mortem examination. Owner of eatery Wafflix, Ali had gone missing on July 28, and his body was found a day later with a gunshot wound in bushes in Karachi’s Gulistan-i-Jauhar. The deceased’s family, along with their lawyer, Jibran Nasir, met members of the new investigation team at the DIG Crime office. The team also met investigators from the previous team and obtained records related to the case. DIG Crime and Investigation Amir Farooqi, who heads the new team, told Dawn that the investigators heard the family and their lawyer in detail about the circumstances surrounding Ali’s murder. “The police will keep the family informed of all steps being taken to solve the case,” he said. He said the new team had obtained the investigation records from the previous team to review the entire case file. Sindh Home Minister Ziaul Hassan Lanjar said earlier today that the provincial government had deferred the decision on the formation of a judicial commission to probe the Mir Raza Ali murder case. Lanjar made the announcement on X, saying that Karachi Mayor Murtaza Wahab had spoken to Ali’s family, who had expressed “confidence in the new police team” constituted to investigate the case and was of the view that it should conduct the probe. “Therefore, the decision of establishing a judicial commission has been deferred for the time being,” the home minister said. While his family was convinced that he was kidnapped, tortured and murdered, police had previously been building the case around the possibility that he died by suicide. A murder charge was eventually added to the first information report after the exhumation and a second postmortem of Ali’s body revealed that he had suffered multiple injuries and was shot in the back, ruling out the possibility of suicide. Controversy fueled by ‘miscommunication’ Sindh Inspector General of Police (IGP) Javed Alam Odho said that the investigation into the murder should be conducted in a better manner, expressing hope that the new investigation team would consider all available evidence. Speaking to the media in Sukkur, he said the government, public and police were all concerned about the case and stressed the need to examine it “with an open mind and open heart”. He said action had been taken against officers found guilty of misconduct and negligence during the investigation. IG Odho said the controversy surrounding Ali’s murder had been fuelled by “miscommunication”. “I have strictly instructed the entire investigation team to keep communication open and transparent this time, whether with the deceased’s family or the media,” he said. On Sunday, PPP leader Faryal Talpur recommended a judicial commission to probe the case, saying it should examine all aspects of the incident and bring the facts to light. A few hours after Talpur’s statement, Lanjar and Wahab had reached Ali’s residence, met with his father, Mir Hussain Ali, and assured the family that they would be provided complete justice. Talking to the media after the meeting, Lanjar had said a decision had been taken to conduct a judicial inquiry, under the supervision of a Sindh High Court judge, into the murder case. However, Jibran Nasir, the family’s lawyer, posted on X that they had not requested or consented to any judicial commission. “Nor do we believe it’s required at this stage. A new investigation team has been formed, which the family will meet tomorrow. The Sindh government should not try to create hurdles/confusion in the name of ‘facilitation,’“ he said. He had earlier also objected to the initially constituted police team probing the case and demanded that it be replaced. Speaking to the media on Saturday after the results of the second autopsy came out, he had said that he and the family had “no faith” in the investigation team. Subsequently, the Sindh inspector general of police’s office notified on Sunday the reconstitution of the investigating team probing the case. The order to this effect said the new investigation team was formed in light of Ali’s second postmortem report, which contradicted the one released after his first postmortem. The same day, Karachi police chief Azad Khan also suspended Sharea Faisal Sub-divisional Police Officer (SDPO) Muhammad Arshad Afridi and Gulistan-i-Jauhar Station House Officer (SHO) Kamran Qureshi with immediate effect for failing to preserve the crime scene and conduct a proper crime-scene investigation after Ali’s body was found. The city police chief also ordered the case be transferred to Zaman Town Police Station from Ferozabad Police Station, where the case was initially registered. Controversy over autopsy The latest developments in the case follow a controversy between the Karachi police surgeon and investigators over alleged loopholes in the medico-legal report regarding Ali’s first post-mortem examination. Karachi Police Surgeon Dr Summaiya Syed told a private news channel last week that the post-mortem findings of Ali’s body had raised several questions, as some observations in the report did not appear to match the available photographs. The police surgeon, whose assessment was based only on the post-mortem report and photographs as she had not examined the body herself back then, had said the reported entry wound, bullet trajectory and exit wound did not correspond with one another. The police surgeon noted that entry wounds were typically smaller than exit wounds in firearm cases. She also said that gunshot residue, commonly found on the hands in suspected suicides, was not tested for in this case. Her interview prompted the police authorities to issue a statement, terming such observations as having the potential to adversely affect the ongoing investigation. The statement, however, said that exhumation of the body could be done on the medical board’s recommendation for further clarification by a committee of medico-legal experts with the court’s permission. On August 6, a judicial magistrate had allowed the exhumation of the body on an application filed by Ali’s father, directing the police surgeon and the Sindh health secretary to constitute a medical board for the exhumation. The Sindh health department then constituted an eight-member board, with Dr Syed as the convener. However, in the early hours of August 7, the board was reconstituted through an order issued by the director general of the Sindh health department. While Dr Syed remained the convener of the new five-member board, its members were changed. But Ali’s family rejected the new board, which also resulted in the deferment of the planned exhumation on Friday. Meanwhile, Nasir accused the authorities of trying to bury the facts. The Sindh government then restored the original medical board, following which Ali’s body was exhumed on Saturday. After a second postmortem of the body, Dr Syed told Dawn that multiple injuries were found on the head and face. “Fractured rib on the back, which is the entry wound of the gunshot [that] exited from the front,” she said. She said the body bore “injuries in the right flank and feet [and] congealed black substance present in the mouth and throat”.

items.title: Accident à Lélouma : deux morts et plusieurs blessés à Thiaguel-Bory
items.description: Un drame de la route a endeuillé à nouveau la préfecture de Lélouma dans la soirée du dimanche 9 août 2026. Un véhicule de transport en commun assurant la liaison entre Labé et la Gambie s'est renversé dans la sous-préfecture de Thiaguel-Bory, faisant deux morts et plusieurs blessés graves, a appris votre quotidien électronique Guinéenews de sources officielles. L'accident est survenu dans le courant de l'après-midi. Alerté par téléphone aux environs de 14 heures, le syndicat des transporteurs s'est rapidement mobilisé en compagnie des forces de l'ordre pour se rendre sur les lieux du drame. Mamadou Bâ Camara, chargé des conflits et des négociations au sein de la CNTG (Confédération nationale des travailleurs de Guinée) de Labé, tente de reconstituer les faits. « Dès que nous avons été informés du renversement de ce véhicule en provenance de Labé pour la Gambie, nous avons saisi le syndicat de Daka et, accompagnés de la gendarmerie, nous nous sommes immédiatement rendus sur place. Nous avons trouvé une première victime déjà décédée et non identifiée. Nous avons aussitôt transporté son corps ainsi que l'ensemble des blessés vers l'hôpital régional de Labé. Malheureusement, un second passager, nommé Adama Oury Diallo et originaire de Lélouma, a succombé à ses blessures à son arrivée à l'hôpital », explique ce responsable syndical. Alors que les premières hypothèses privilégient une défaillance du système de freinage, les constatations faites sur le terrain orientent désormais les enquêteurs vers un problème mécanique bien précis. Selon les précisions du représentant syndical, c'est une panne au niveau de la boîte de vitesses qui serait à l'origine de la perte de contrôle du véhicule, une Renault 21 qui transportait à son bord neuf passagers et le chauffeur. Actuellement, les blessés sont tous pris en charge à l'hôpital régional de Labé. Les dépouilles des deux victimes ont été déposées à la morgue du même établissement.

items.title: Après les événements de Sebta, Rome et Copenhague plaident pour des centres de retour hors de l’UE
items.description: Les conséquences des récents événements survenus dans l'enclave occupée de Sebta continuent de résonner au sein de l’Union européenne. Dans une déclaration commune, la présidente du Conseil italien, Giorgia Meloni, et la Première ministre danoise, Mette Frederiksen, ont appelé à un renforcement de la politique européenne en matière d’immigration irrégulière, allant jusqu’à proposer la création de centres de retour pour migrants dans des pays tiers situés hors du territoire européen. Le texte, publié dans un contexte marqué par les arrivées massives de migrants depuis le Maroc vers la ville de Sebta occupée, souligne le rejet par Rome et Copenhague de ce que les deux dirigeantes qualifient d’« immigration incontrôlée » vers l’Europe. Elles y défendent la nécessité d’explorer de nouvelles approches pour faire face à l’immigration irrégulière. « Nous n’acceptons pas une immigration incontrôlée vers l’Europe et nous avons œuvré au renforcement d’une politique migratoire stricte, tant dans nos pays qu’au niveau européen », affirment Giorgia Meloni et Mette Frederiksen dans ce document. Une convergence politique autour de la question migratoire Les deux responsables reconnaissent que leurs positions ne coïncident pas sur l’ensemble des dossiers européens. Elles soulignent néanmoins partager une même vision lorsqu’il s’agit de la gestion des frontières et de la maîtrise des flux migratoires. « Nous sommes les deux seules femmes cheffes de gouvernement au sein de l’Union européenne. L’une dirige un grand pays du Sud, l’autre un petit pays du Nord, mais nous avons en commun la volonté de défendre l’Europe », écrivent-elles. Selon les deux dirigeantes, l’immigration irrégulière produit des effets négatifs sur les sociétés européennes. Elles évoquent notamment une augmentation de certaines formes de criminalité, une pression croissante sur les services publics ainsi qu’une érosion de la confiance des citoyens dans les institutions. Leur analyse se veut plus sévère encore lorsque des personnes ne disposant pas d’un droit de séjour sont impliquées dans des crimes violents, le trafic de stupéfiants ou des violences sexuelles. Dans ce contexte, elles estiment que les gouvernements européens ont l’obligation d’apporter des « réponses concrètes » aux citoyens, en particulier aux populations les plus vulnérables, afin de renforcer leur sécurité. Le projet de centres de retour hors de l’Union européenne La proposition la plus marquante de la déclaration concerne la création de « centres de retour dans des pays tiers », destinés à accueillir les personnes ne bénéficiant pas d’un droit de résidence au sein de l’Union européenne. Les deux responsables citent l’exemple de l’Albanie, où l’Italie a déjà développé un dispositif de ce type. Elles indiquent également que des initiatives comparables sont actuellement étudiées dans plusieurs pays africains. À travers cette orientation, Rome et Copenhague entendent déplacer une partie des mécanismes de gestion de l’immigration irrégulière en dehors des frontières européennes, rompant ainsi avec une approche fondée exclusivement sur des dispositifs internes à l’Union. Les deux dirigeantes insistent par ailleurs sur le fait que le respect des lois doit s’accompagner du respect des valeurs européennes, un principe qui, selon elles, doit s’appliquer aussi bien aux migrants en situation irrégulière qu’aux étrangers résidant légalement sur le continent. « Le respect de nos lois doit aller de pair avec le respect des valeurs européennes », soulignent-elles. Les événements de Ceuta relancent le débat européen Cette prise de position intervient alors que les événements de Sebta ont ravivé les débats européens autour des questions migratoires. Dans leur sillage, l’Italie a instauré des contrôles visant les voyageurs en provenance d’Espagne dans ses aéroports et ses ports. Madrid a ensuite adopté des mesures similaires à l’égard des voyageurs arrivant d’Italie, après le refus des autorités italiennes de lever ces restrictions. Ces décisions illustrent l’ampleur des répercussions des événements survenus à Sebta. Celles-ci dépassent désormais le seul cadre du préside pour toucher la circulation des personnes entre plusieurs États européens, au moment où les discussions sur le contrôle des frontières, les politiques de retour et la gestion de l’immigration irrégulière occupent une place croissante dans l’agenda politique de l’Union. Une référence assumée à l’identité européenne Au-delà des considérations sécuritaires et juridiques, la déclaration commune aborde également la question des valeurs et de l’identité européenne. Giorgia Meloni et Mette Frederiksen revendiquent l’héritage culturel chrétien de l’Europe et affirment que les personnes choisissant de s’y installer doivent respecter les principes qui, selon elles, fondent les sociétés européennes. Pour les deux dirigeantes, la maîtrise de l’immigration irrégulière passe ainsi autant par l’application des règles de droit que par l’adhésion aux valeurs communes qu’elles considèrent constitutives du projet européen. Cette vision accompagne leur appel à un durcissement des mesures visant les personnes ne disposant pas du droit de séjour dans les États membres, les centres de retour installés dans des pays tiers étant présentés comme l’un des principaux outils susceptibles d’être mobilisés dans ce cadre. The post Après les événements de Sebta, Rome et Copenhague plaident pour des centres de retour hors de l’UE appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Sahara : la Colombie répond au polisario et réaffirme sa reconnaissance de la souveraineté marocaine
items.description: Le ministère colombien des Affaires étrangères a officiellement réagi aux affirmations des partisans du polisario concernant sa décision de retirer sa reconnaissance à la pseudo « république arabe sahraouie démocratique » (rasd). Dans un communiqué consulté par Hespress, la diplomatie colombienne précise que « la décision a été prise à la suite d’un réexamen souverain de la reconnaissance de la RASD accordée par le gouvernement précédent, en tenant compte du fait que les Nations unies ne la reconnaissent pas comme un État membre, et dans le cadre du renforcement du partenariat stratégique de la Colombie avec le Royaume du Maroc ». Le communiqué ajoute que la Colombie reconnaît la souveraineté du Maroc sur l’ensemble de son territoire, y compris le Sahara. Dans ce contexte, le gouvernement colombien a décidé de geler ses relations avec la « rasd » à compter de cette date. Cela signifie, selon la même source, qu’il n’y aura plus de contacts politiques ou diplomatiques, ni d’échanges de représentations, ni de soutien à la « rasd » dans les instances multilatérales, notamment aux Nations unies et au Conseil de sécurité, où la Colombie siège actuellement en tant que membre non permanent. Le communiqué poursuit : « Cette décision respecte pleinement le droit international, la Charte des Nations unies ainsi que le cadre proposé par la résolution 2797 (2025) du Conseil de sécurité sur le Sahara. » Selon le document, cette nouvelle orientation confirme également la volonté de la Colombie de relancer ses relations avec le Maroc, son allié depuis près de cinquante ans, sur la base d’une vision à long terme et avec la volonté de construire une relation renouvelée, dans laquelle le rapprochement bilatéral servirait pleinement les intérêts du peuple colombien. La nouvelle dynamique bilatérale entre la Colombie et le Maroc, poursuit le communiqué, reposera sur une coopération ambitieuse et concrète, offrant un important potentiel dans les domaines des échanges commerciaux, de la promotion des investissements, du tourisme, de la sécurité alimentaire, du développement portuaire et de la logistique, ainsi que du renforcement de la connectivité atlantique entre les deux pays. Vendredi dernier, la Colombie avait annoncé un changement de position concernant la question du Sahara, affirmant reconnaître la souveraineté du Royaume du Maroc sur ses provinces du Sud. Cette nouvelle position avait été annoncée lors d’une rencontre entre Nasser Bourita, ministre des Affaires étrangères, et José Manuel Restrepo, vice-président de la République de Colombie, en présence d’Álvaro Leyva Escobar, ministre des Relations extérieures. À cette occasion, Leyva Escobar avait affirmé que la Colombie « reconnaît la souveraineté du Maroc sur son Sahara » , consacrant ainsi une nouvelle orientation de la position colombienne sur cette question. De son côté, Restrepo avait déclaré que cette annonce constituait un « nouveau départ » dans les relations entre la Colombie et le Maroc, soulignant que le Royaume était considéré comme « le principal allié de la Colombie en Afrique ». Le vice-président colombien avait également exprimé la volonté de son pays d’établir un partenariat stratégique avec le Maroc. Pour sa part, Bourita avait qualifié de « historique » la décision de la Colombie de retirer sa reconnaissance à la prétendue « République arabe sahraouie démocratique » et de reconnaître la souveraineté du Maroc sur son Sahara, estimant que cette décision devrait donner « un nouvel élan » aux relations bilatérales. Le ministre des Affaires étrangères a également souligné que le Maroc et la Colombie pourraient constituer des plateformes économiques réciproques, en tirant parti de leurs positions stratégiques respectives en Afrique et en Amérique latine. Bourita a enfin indiqué que sa présence à Cali, sur Hautes Instructions du Roi Mohammed VI, pour représenter le souverain lors de la cérémonie d’investiture du nouveau président Abelardo de la Espriella, reflétait la volonté du Royaume d’accompagner cette nouvelle dynamique et de porter les relations maroco-colombiennes à un niveau supérieur. items.title: Procès de Ras Bath et Rose vie chère, les débats s’ouvrent devant la Cour d’appel
items.description: Le proces de Mohamed Youssouf Bathily, alias « Ras Bath », et de Rokia Doumbia, dite « Rose vie chere », s'est ouvert ce lundi 10 août devant la chambre criminelle de la Cour d'appel de Bamako. Les deux accuses sont poursuivis pour association de malfaiteurs et atteinte au credit de l'etat par le biais des TIC. L'audience s'est deroulee devant une salle pleine. L'audience a debute par le visionnage de l'emission au cours de laquelle Ras Bath avait recu Rokia Doumbia en tant qu'activiste. Les echanges se sont ensuite poursuivis entre le procureur general et Ras Bath. a la barre, ce dernier a defendu son droit de critiquer le regime et de denoncer la hausse des prix des produits de premiere necessite. Le procureur general a, de son cote, rappele que la liberte s'exerce dans les limites fixees par la loi. Il a estime que l'emission visait a discrediter le regime. Il a notamment releve que la Direction generale du commerce, de la concurrence et de la consommation (DGCC) n'avait pas ete invitee a l'emission. Les echanges entre les deux parties ont parfois ete houleux. Rose vie chere rejette les accusations a la barre, Rokia Doumbia, dite « Rose vie chere », a rejete les accusations portees contre elle. Rokia Doumbia affirme avoir agi dans une demarche citoyenne. Son objectif, selon elle, etait d'alerter les autorites sur la cherte de la vie et la hausse des prix des produits de premiere necessite. « Je suis commercante et non militante politique », a-t-elle declare. Elle a ainsi refute toute volonte de renverser le regime. L'audience se poursuit Les debats se poursuivent devant la chambre criminelle de la Cour d'appel de Bamako. Le tribunal devra examiner les differents elements du dossier avant de se prononcer sur les accusations portees contre les deux prevenus. items.title: El mundo del fútbol estrecha la presión sobre Infantino
items.description: El mundo del fútbol acrecentó este lunes la presión sobre el presidente de la FIFA, el cuestionado Gianni Infantino. Por la mañana, la UEFA, la Confederación Asiática de Fútbol (AFC) y la Confederación de Norteamérica, Centroamérica y el Caribe de Fútbol (Concacaf) publicaron una primera carta conjunta contra el dirigente ítalo-suizo en la que afirman que este rompió “mediante el engaño” la confianza en la cúpula del organismo que rige el fútbol mundial con su fallida propuesta de constituir una sociedad llamada FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) para explotar comercialmente las Copas del Mundo masculinas y femeninas con un 20% de capital privado. Poco después, la Asociación Transparencia y Democracia en el Deporte, encabezada por Miguel Galán, el hombre que logró que con sus querellas cayeran los expresidentes de la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) Ángel María Villar y Pedro Rocha, presentó una denuncia ante la Comisión Ética de la FIFA para que esta investigue a su mandamás. El texto, adelantado por EL PAÍS, pide que se abra un procedimiento contra Infantino para determinar si cometió alguna infracción en su rechazado plan para explotar los derechos del Mundial, en la creación y entrega del Premio de la Paz de la FIFA a Donald Trump y en el caso Balogun , es decir, la inédita retirada de una tarjeta rota al estadounidense Florian Balogun durante el Mundial tras una llamada del presidente estadounidense para que el delantero pudiera jugar los octavos de final ante Bélgica. items.title: PTI leadership, TTAP on board for September 27 long march to Islamabad: Sohail Afridi
items.description: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi on Monday said PTI’s political leadership and its ally, the Tehreek Tahaffuz-i-Ayeen Pakistan (TTAP), were on board with the call for a long march to Islamabad on September 27. Speaking on Geo News programme ‘Capital Talk’, CM Afridi said, “The PTI’s political leadership across the country and its ally, the TTAP, are all on board with the long march, and they collectively agreed on September 27 as the date for it.” Responding to a question about Imran Khan’s sister Aleema Khan’s reservations over the date, he said she was a “non-political individual” and would agree to the date once the PTI apprised her of all the facts and figures. CM Afridi also denied allegations by a PTI member currently residing outside Pakistan that he had met Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi before finalising the date for the long march. “That allegation was rubbish. At the time of the alleged meeting, I was at KP House in Islamabad, contrary to the claim that I had met him in Peshawar,” he said. In response to a question, CM Afridi also rejected the impression of a communication gap between the party’s leadership and workers. Talking about the ‘D-Chowk, D-Chowk’ slogans during the recent Peshawar rally , he said institutions that were not granting political space to the PTI should understand that the party’s leadership had taken on a great burden by seeking to resolve issues through mutual understanding. “However, not just in KP but across Pakistan, particularly the youth, no one will be able to contain them when they come out on Sept 27, because I can see passion and a ray of light in their eyes,” the chief minister said. During the interview, the KP chief minister also criticised the federal government led by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif for economic inefficiency and bad governance. He said that if he met the PTI founder at Adiala jail and was instructed to defer the Sept 27 date for the long march, he would agree. CM Afridi added that he would also follow Imran’s instructions if asked to pave the way for talks. At the outset of his interview, Afridi said the PTI had no option but to protest as its grievances were not being heard by the authorities. “People say that the PTI does politics of chaos, unrest and protests; however, it would not have resorted to these if it had been heard by the authorities.” He claimed Imran had been jailed unlawfully. “The PTI founder is in solitary confinement and denied his rights. No one is allowed to meet him — not me, his family, lawyers or personal physicians.” After exhausting all constitutional and legal means, he said, the PTI had no other option but to protest. “We are holding a peaceful protest. The Constitution allows us to do so, so the authorities will have to hear us.” He reiterated that the PTI wanted justice for its founder and wanted his cases to be heard on merit, with access to his personal doctors and quality medical treatment. He further claimed that the KP police had faced interference from the federal government and other institutions. The chief minister also distanced the provincial government from cases registered against journalists in KP, saying it would never allow such actions. On a proposal to create new provinces in Pakistan, CM Afridi said it was the PTI founder’s vision to establish new administrative units across the country. “But the question is: who will create them? Only a government with a mandate can do so,” he said, adding, “We support the call for creating new administrative units, but only through a government brought to power by the people.” Imran — imprisoned since Aug 5, 2023 — is serving a 14-year sentence at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail in the £190m case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case . An accountability court in Islamabad had sentenced Imran and Bushra to 14 and seven years in prison, respectively, on Jan 17, 2025, in the case. Subsequently, both had challenged their convictions before the IHC. The case alleges that the couple obtained billions of rupees and land worth hundreds of kanals from Bahria Town Ltd to legalise Rs50 billion identified and returned to the country by the United Kingdom during the PTI government.

items.title: Course au secrétariat général de l’ONU: la dernière ligne droite pour Macky Sall
items.description: Ceci est une tribune du Dr Ablassé Ouédraogo ancien haut fonctionnaire des Nations Unies et ancien ministre des Affaires étrangères du Burkina Faso, portant sur le choix du nouveau Secrétaire général de l’Organisation des Nations Unies dont l'ex-président sénégalais Macky Sall est candidat. Le nouveau Secrétaire général de l’Organisation des Nations Unies, qui succédera à António Guterres le 1er janvier 2027, sera officiellement nommé par la 81ᵉ Assemblée Générale des Nations Unies qui ouvre ses travaux le 8 septembre 2026 au siège de l’Organisation à New York. La Charte des Nations Unies stipule que la désignation du Secrétaire général s’effectue sur recommandation du Conseil de sécurité, nécessitant le vote favorable d’au moins neuf (9) de ses quinze membres, sans veto de l’un des cinq membres permanents (Chine, États-Unis, France, Royaume-Uni et Russie). Les membres non permanents représentant actuellement l’Afrique au Conseil de sécurité sont le Libéria, la République démocratique du Congo et la Somalie. En prélude à cette désignation, un premier vote indicatif ou «straw poll» s’est tenu le 30 juillet 2026. D’autres consultations suivront avant le choix définitif du Conseil de sécurité. Le vote indicatif vise à évaluer le rapport de force entre les prétendants. Exercice purement consultatif, il ne constitue ni une élection officielle ni une décision irrévocable. Son rôle essentiel est d’identifier et de lever les réticences des puissances disposant du droit de veto, tout en permettant aux candidats et à leurs partisans d’évaluer le chemin restant à parcourir. Le président Macky Sall se positionne comme le principal prétendant du continent africain pour succéder à António Guterres à la tête de l’ONU. En dépit d'un premier vote indicatif peu favorable le 30 juillet dernier, le candidat Macky Sall demeure pleinement engagé dans la course et conserve toutes ses chances. Le processus de désignation reposant traditionnellement sur la recherche d'un consensus, Macky Sall prévaut d'un parcours diplomatique éprouvé au cours de ses douze années à la tête du Sénégal. Ce profil rassembleur apparaît en mesure d’emporter l'adhésion tant des puissances occidentales que de la Chine et de la Russie. Fort d'une solide expérience des négociations internationales, il entretient d'excellentes relations avec l'ensemble des membres permanents du Conseil de sécurité grâce à une diplomatie mesurée et pragmatique. Cette posture lui offre un accès privilégié auprès de tous les acteurs clés ; toutefois, la décision finale appartiendra souverainement au Conseil de sécurité. Fait notable, le Président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Faye a officialisé, le 21 juillet 2026, le soutien du Sénégal à la candidature de Macky Sall, mobilisant ainsi le réseau diplomatique de l’État pour appuyer sa campagne. La capacité du candidat africain à diriger l’ONU ne suscite aucun doute au regard de son parcours d'exception. Ancien Président de la République, Premier ministre, Président de l’Assemblée nationale du Sénégal, ministre, ainsi qu'ancien président de la CEDEAO et de l’Union africaine, Macky Sall possède une maîtrise approfondie de la gouvernance politique et institutionnelle. Ces qualités s'avèrent indispensables pour le futur Secrétaire général, appelé à restaurer la confiance au sein d'une communauté internationale en pleine mutation. Dans le contexte géopolitique actuel, Macky Sall a su convaincre lors des auditions consacrées à sa vision des trois piliers des Nations Unies, à savoir la paix et la sécurité, les droits de l’homme, et le développement. Ses propositions de réformes structurelles visant à résorber les crises de confiance et de financement de l’Organisation démontrent sa capacité à rétablir le dialogue entre les grands acteurs mondiaux et à revitaliser le multilatéralisme. La démarche stratégique de Macky Sall vise précisément à refonder la gouvernance mondiale autour de ce triptyque : paix, sécurité et développement durable. Lors des échanges interactifs d’avril et de juillet 2026, il a placé sa candidature sous le signe d’un multilatéralisme réinventé, destiné à redonner à l’ONU toute sa capacité d’action au service des nations. L’échéance décisive interviendra dans les toutes prochaines semaines. Il appartient désormais à Macky Sall et à ses appuis de redoubler d’efforts pour concrétiser cette ambition, afin de restaurer la confiance, la cohérence et l’équité dans les relations entre le Nord et le Sud. N’en déplaise aux courants afro-pessimistes qui invoquent le principe de rotation régionale — règle informelle qui ne figure nulle part dans la Charte —la dynamique engagée par le candidat Macky Sall demeure solide et prometteuse pour l'issue du processus de sélection. Rappelons enfin que l'autorité et les responsabilités relèvent, en dernier ressort, de la volonté du Tout-Puissant. Que Dieu exauce nos vœux. Ouagadougou, le 10 août 2026 Dr Ablassé OUÉDRAOGO Ancien Ministre des Affaires étrangères du Burkina Faso Ancien Président du Conseil des Ministres de l’Organisation de l’Unité Africaine (OUA) Ancien Directeur général adjoint de l’Organisation mondiale du commerce (OMC) Ancien Haut fonctionnaire des Nations Unies L’article Course au secrétariat général de l'ONU: la dernière ligne droite pour Macky Sall est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .
